445	## Formulas
446	
447	Nothing in this section is hashed, replicated or saved: the HUD owns no simulation state (HS-1), so the kernel's determinism rule (integer-only, `rng_derive`, `state_hash`) does not bind these formulas. They are nevertheless written in **integer arithmetic wherever that is cheap** (`div` is floor division, `ceil_div(a, b) = (a + b - 1) div b`), because ADR candidate G requires the HUD maths to be pure static functions that a headless gdUnit4 run can assert exactly without a renderer. Two formulas use real numbers because they describe motion that is never compared bit for bit (`hud_settle_response`, `cancel_drain_fill`). Formulas owned by this GDD are D.1 to D.16; D.17 to D.20 are neighbours' formulas, cited by their owners' ids with their verbatim outputs and never redefined. "HUD px" is one art pixel at HUD scale `H` (one HUD px = `H` screen px). Every name below is registered at Phase 5 from this text; the HUD-owned constants are `[PH]` and their ranges are in Tuning Knobs.
448	
449	### D.1 strip_budget (HS-11, HS-15; registered, two bounds)
450	
451	The strip_budget formula is defined as:
452	
453	`W_content = 2*B + 2*G + 2*P_in + W_arc + W_num + W_mark ; W_num = 3*A + 2*LS ; H_content = 2*B + H_interior ; slack_w = W_cap - W_content >= 0 ; slack_h = H_cap - H_content >= 0 ; W_cap = (STRIP_MAX_W_PCT * 640) div 100 ; H_cap = (STRIP_MAX_H_PCT * 360) div 100`
454	
455	**Variables:**
456	
457	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
458	|---|---|---|---|---|
459	| `B` | int HUD px | 1 | art-director frame geometry | Plate border width (Graphite lit hairline) |
460	| `G` | int HUD px | 1-3 | UX spec (`[PH]` 2) | Gap between the arc, the numeral and the mark slot (two gaps) |
461	| `P_in` | int HUD px | 0-2 | UX spec (`[PH]` 0) | Inner padding of the plate |
462	| `W_arc` | int HUD px | 20-28 | UX spec (`[PH]` 24) | Width of the dial-arc cell including the pivot cap |
463	| `A`, `LS` | int HUD px | A 5-6, LS 1 | instrument face (does not yet exist; `[PH]` 5 and 1) | Tabular digit advance and letter-spacing of the 7-cap face |
464	| `W_num` | int HUD px | 15-20 | derived | Three tabular digit columns: `3*A + 2*LS` = 17 |
465	| `W_mark` | int HUD px | 16 | art bible 7.2 (the 16 x 16 cell includes its 1-px clearance; live 14 x 14) | The always-reserved mark slot |
466	| `H_interior` | int HUD px | 16 | art-director (the mark fills it) | Interior height of the strip |
467	| `STRIP_MAX_W_PCT`, `STRIP_MAX_H_PCT` | int % | 12, 5 | art bible ab:751 (user decision), cited | The cap, defined at the 1080p reference canvas (640 x 360 HUD px) |
468	| `W_cap`, `H_cap` | int HUD px | 76, 18 | derived | The cap in HUD px; 76 is `floor(76.8)`; 18 is exact |
469	
470	**Output Range:** `slack_w` and `slack_h` are integers, both required `>= 0` at every `H`, because the strip is authored in HUD px. The strip fails the budget when `W_num > 30` at the default other widths (`76 - (63 - 17)`). The cap is knowingly exceeded in *screen* terms at `H > H_default` and on the Steam Deck (HS-15); the invariant is in HUD px.
471	
472	**Example:** the default content is `2*1 + 2*2 + 2*0 + 24 + 17 + 16 = 63` HUD px, so `slack_w = 76 - 63 = 13`; with the conservative 18-px mark slot the content is 65 and the slack is 11. Height: `2*1 + 16 = 18`, `slack_h = 0` (zero slack: any frame-border change breaks the cap). Adding a 16 x 16 O2 loop glyph gives `63 + 16 = 79` (or 83 with its gap) `> 76`, which is why HS-11 omits it. A second 16-px mark slot for the ship-alarm mark overflows the same way (`63 + 16 = 79`), which is why HS-22 puts that slot on the suit panel *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. Every width is provisional on the instrument face (risk R-9): a face with `A` 6 gives `W_num` 20 and content 66, still inside.
473	
474	### D.2 hud_flash_budget (HS-14, HS-45, HS-47; registered, with the honest-tick floor)
475	
476	The hud_flash_budget formula is defined as:
477	
478	`admit(e, t) = TRUE iff for every window end w in W(t): N(w) + [e counts in w] <= FLASH_MAX_PER_S ; W(t) = {t} U {tick of every clock-locked event already scheduled in (t, t + TICK_RATE)} ; N(w) = number of luminance events, admitted or clock-locked, with tick in (w - TICK_RATE, w]` and `honest_tick_floor_ms(u) = ceil_div(1000 * BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS, FLASH_MAX_PER_S * BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS - u * TICK_RATE)` with `u` = 1; **user rulings D91 (ii), (iv) and D79 add** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: `flash_weight_pm(e) = ceil_div(1000 * 9 * area_px(e), canvas_w_int * canvas_h_int)` ; `exempt(e, t) = (flash_mode == WEIGHTED) AND (class(e) in {DIGIT_SWAP, PROMPT_SHOW_START}) AND (flash_weight_pm(e) + X(t) < FLASH_AREA_EXEMPT_PM)` ; `X(t) = sum of flash_weight_pm over the exempt events with tick in (t - TICK_RATE, t]` ; an exempt event is admitted at once and is added to no `N(w)`; every other event, and every event in STRICT mode, goes through `admit`
479	
480	**Variables:**
481	
482	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
483	|---|---|---|---|---|
484	| `e` | event | prompt show-start (and the give_up plate show-start, HS-42(b), which takes the prompt's WEIGHTED exemption test but is never deferred, HS-47 *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*), honest grid boundary (skip-only), notice or scanner show-start, state-display draw (the lamp glyph, tool bracket, glowstick count, TAP relabel: HS-47 class A, coalesced by the shared limiter) | HUD | A deferrable HUD-owned luminance event (a boundary with no displayed digit change is not an event; a grid boundary is admitted at its own tick or skipped, never delayed, and never skipped twice in a row) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
485	| `MAX_DEFER_TICKS` | int ticks | 60 `[PH]` (range 30-120) | this GDD (HUD-owned, unregistered until Phase 5) | The longest a deferrable event may wait for room; on expiry it is force-admitted and counted (overrun, `HUD_FLASH_OVERRUN`). 60 is one full window, the longest wait that a window of deferrable-only load can impose; below 30 the guarantee degenerates into overrun *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
486	| `GLYPH_STATE_LATCH_TICKS` | int ticks | 20 `[PH]` (range 20-60) | this GDD | The minimum gap between two admitted state-display draws across the whole class (HS-47 class A); formerly the lamp glyph's own latch *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
487	| `t`, `w` | int ticks | 0.. | kernel `T` | The candidate tick and each forward window end; windows are half-open `(w - 60, w]` |
488	| `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` | int | 3 | Render Pipeline PR-13 (locked), cited | Luminance changes per rolling second per HUD |
489	| `TICK_RATE` | int | 60 | kernel (locked), cited | Ticks per second, the window length |
490	| `BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS` | int ticks | 128 (range 120-180) | Emitter State (registry), cited | The mark's period by relation; worst-case arithmetic uses the range floor 120 |
491	| `u` | int | 1 (the ruled unit; 2, the edge unit, is retired) | user ruling D91 (ii): a flash is a pair of opposing transitions, counted `ceil(n_transitions / 2)` (registry `flash_count`) | How many luminance events one mark cycle counts as: 1 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* |
492	| `flash_mode` | enum | STRICT, WEIGHTED | `HudSettings.reduce_flashing`: STRICT while on (on at first launch, user ruling D79), WEIGHTED while off | Which events the arbiter counts *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* |
493	| `area_px(e)` | int HUD px | 35 (one 5 x 7 digit cell) to about 2,160 | the changed rectangle: a grid boundary is the digit cells that change (up to 6 cells, 210 px, when the O2 and reserve numerals both change, EC-HS-21); a prompt show-start is the plate rectangle (`PROMPT_PLATE_MAX_W_PX` 72 by 12 for ENABLED, 18 for NEEDS_TOOL, 30 for a grown two-line plate) | Pixels whose luminance the event changes (every changed pixel is taken as a full-scale change, the worst case) |
494	| `canvas_w_int`, `canvas_h_int` | int HUD px | `P_w div H`, `P_h div H` (640 x 360 at 1080p, `H` 3) | Render Pipeline, `H` | The HUD canvas; one region is a ninth of it (registry `flash_count`: region = a ninth of the displayed picture) |
495	| `FLASH_AREA_EXEMPT_PM` | int permille | 100 (range 50-100, never above 100) | the Pipeline's rule that a transition counts at a 10 % area-weighted change (registry `flash_count`) | Below this a flash is sub-threshold *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* |
496	| `HONEST_TICK_MS`, `HONEST_GRID_TICKS` | int ms; int ticks | 500 (pinned; the 400-500 range is withdrawn), `HONEST_GRID_TICKS = HONEST_TICK_MS * TICK_RATE div 1000` = 30 | this GDD | The shared honest-numeral hold grid (HS-14), **anchored to the committed tick** (`T mod HONEST_GRID_TICKS == 0`); also used by the inspect card's numeral. The registry's restatement of the Instruments grid in wall milliseconds (`t_grid(j) = j * HONEST_TICK_MS` on `present_time`) is to be restated in ticks (cross-GDD note to Instruments). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
497	| `T_tick` | int ms | 400 / 668 / 1002 / 1336 | Filter `lying_digit_tick_schedule`, cited (D.20) | Lying-digit period; never rescheduled by the HUD |
498	
499	Non-deferrable events (hides, mark leading edges, Filter lying-digit ticks, source-state hue cuts and the breath-source swap, orphan transitions, and the class-B acknowledgement cues of HS-47 (ACK plus force-admitted show-start, reject hold, OUTCOME step); the class-A state displays are deferrable) always happen *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; the honest grid boundary is clock-locked and skip-only (its tick is fixed, it may be skipped, it is never delayed). Mark leading edges, lying-digit ticks and source-state hue cuts (HSV-4, L-5: a glyph or arc band changing between its loop hue and Graphite lit; counted, never deferred, because they follow the honest source state) always count. Under the ruled unit (`u` = 1) a hide is not a counted event (the edge unit, which counted it as the trailing edge of its show-start's cycle, is retired). **Priority among HUD-owned deferrable events:** prompt show-start, then honest grid boundary (skip-only), then notice or scanner show-start, then the state-display class. The grid boundary is clock-locked, so it is *scheduled first* into every window that `admit` tests (it is in `W(t)` before any prompt asks); "the prompt outranks the grid" means only that a boundary is skipped to make room for a waiting prompt, which is the order HS-47 states (this reconciles the earlier example line that read as allocating the grid first). **Grid-skip rule:** a boundary that would exceed the budget while a prompt waits is skipped (never delayed) **but never twice in a row**; the next boundary shows the then-latest value; numeral lag is bounded by `2 x HONEST_TICK_MS` unconditionally. A prompt waits at most one grid cell **only with at most one other counted event in the window**; in general it waits at most `MAX_DEFER_TICKS` and is then force-admitted and counted (the bounds of HS-47 are stated with these preconditions) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
500	
501	**Counting unit and its bound (user ruling D91 (ii))** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: let a window hold `m` **complete pairs** (two opposing transitions inside the window, counted once at the leading edge: a mark cycle's ON and OFF edges, or a plate's show-start and its hide), `k` **single-transition events** (a grid boundary, a substitution, a show-start whose hide lies after the window, a mark ON edge whose OFF edge lies after it) and `o` **orphan transitions** (a hide, or a mark OFF edge, whose leading edge lies before the window; *new, re-review*). Then `n = 2m + k + o` transitions, the ruled flash count is `ceil(n / 2) = m + ceil((k + o) / 2)`, and the arbiter's count is `E = m + k + o`, so `ceil(n / 2) <= E` for every `k, o >= 0`: keeping `E <= FLASH_MAX_PER_S` keeps the ruled count at or below it. *(The earlier statement counted a hide as nothing and so assumed `o` = 0: a window with orphan hides at its edges, hide, show, hide, show, hide, show, hide, holds 7 transitions, ruled count `ceil(7 / 2)` = 4, while `E` counted only the three show-starts, so the arbiter passed a window the ruling forbids. The orphan hide is now counted from the tick it occurs, as a non-deferrable event, so the next show-start is refused while it stands; the first orphan of a run can still overrun by one, recorded as `HUD_FLASH_OVERRUN`, because a hide is immediate and unpredictable, AC-HS-142.)* Worked example: two numeral boundaries and one mark cycle in a window give `n = 4` (or 3 with only the ON edge inside it), the ruled count is 2, and `E` is 3, so the margin is one flash; the seven-transition window above gives `n = 7`, ruled 4, `E` = 4 once the orphan hide is counted, which is over the ceiling and refused. The literal `ceil(n / 2)` would admit up to six single transitions per second; the HUD does not use that headroom (it would unpin the grid proof and the Filter counts its own ticks).
502	
503	**Weighted exemption (user ruling D91 (iv); creative-director exemptions)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: a flash is weighted by the area it covers (WCAG 2.3.1), measured as the registry's region, a ninth of the displayed picture, with every changed pixel taken as a full-scale change so that the weight can only be over-stated. An event is sub-threshold when `flash_weight_pm < FLASH_AREA_EXEMPT_PM` (100, the Pipeline's 10 % area-weighted transition). Exactly two classes can be exempt, and only in WEIGHTED mode: honest-numeral digit swaps and prompt show-starts. The Alarm Red mark is never exempt (its edges are counted strictly in both modes, red flash included), and in STRICT mode (reduce flashing) nothing is exempt. A **cumulative guard** keeps the exemption from becoming a loophole: WCAG sums the area of concurrent flashes, so an event is exempt only while the rolling-second sum `X(t)` of exempt weights plus its own stays below the threshold; otherwise it is counted and goes through `admit` (it is returned to the strict arithmetic, never dropped). **Worked weights** (every figure is `ceil_div(9000 * area_px, canvas_w_int * canvas_h_int)`): the six-cell numeral change (210 px) weighs 9 at 1080p `H` 3 (canvas 640 x 360 = 230,400), 19 on the Steam Deck and at 720p `H` 3 (canvas 426 x 240 = 102,240) and 33 at 1080p `H` 6 (320 x 180 = 57,600), all far below 100. **The Deck's picture mode is pinned to `keep`** (the Pipeline's default until its spike steps pass: a 1280 x 720 picture with 40-px bars in the 1280 x 800 window, HUD canvas 426.67 x 240, integer canvas 426 x 240), so every Deck figure in this GDD equals the 720p `H` 3 figure; the earlier mixed use of a 426 x 266 canvas (`expand`, post-spike) for some weights and 426.67 x 240 for others is retired, and `expand` (canvas height 266.67) can only add vertical room *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. The ENABLED plate (72 x 12 = 864 px) weighs 34, 60, 94 and 135 at 1080p `H` 3, 4, 5 and 6 and 77 on the Deck and at 720p `H` 3 (canvas 426 x 240). The NEEDS_TOOL plate (72 x 18 = 1,296 px) weighs 51 and 90 at 1080p `H` 3 and 4, 141 at `H` 5, and 115 on the Deck and at 720p. A grown two-line plate (72 x 30 = 2,160 px) weighs 85 at 1080p `H` 3 and 150 at `H` 4. So a prompt show-start is exempt for the ENABLED plate through `H` 5 on 1080p and on the Deck and at 720p, for the NEEDS_TOOL plate at `H` 3 and 4 on 1080p only (on the Deck and at 720p it is counted, as a first-priority deferrable event), and for a grown two-line plate at 1080p `H` 3 only. **Flag for the UX spec:** the 24 / 18 reading-face tier grows the plates (C-I), so the exemption must be re-checked against the drawn plates, and the table above is the test.
504	
505	**Output Range:** `admit` is a boolean. For HUD-owned deferrable events `N(w) <= FLASH_MAX_PER_S` always holds; it can be exceeded only by non-deferrable events (Filter ticks at Vertical Slice A, a source-state hue cut or breath-source swap, an orphan hide, a class-B acknowledgement cue landing in an already-full window) and by a deferrable event force-admitted at `MAX_DEFER_TICKS`, which the HUD counts as `HUD_FLASH_OVERRUN` and does not alter; the class-A state displays are coalesced by the shared limiter and so cannot be raised above the ceiling by input alone *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. `honest_tick_floor_ms` is an integer in 375 to 400 (`u` = 1) over the whole `BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS` range: it is the **average-rate** floor, necessary but not sufficient, because `admit` tests a rolling 60-tick window. **Window feasibility (the validator's check, not a static range):** with the grid every `g` ticks a 60-tick window holds `ceil(60 / g)` boundaries at most (3 when `g` < 30, exactly 2 when `g` = 30); plus the mark's counted edges in the window (1 under the ruled `u` = 1) the total must not exceed `FLASH_MAX_PER_S`. At `g` = 30 and `u` = 1: 2 + 1 = 3 (feasible); at `g` = 24: 3 + 1 = 4 (infeasible). So `HONEST_TICK_MS` is pinned at 500 and the data validator **recomputes the check at the live `BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS` and `u`** and fails the data file when it is infeasible. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Since the mode rulings (D79, D91 (iv)), counted numerals and a pulsing mark coexist only rarely** (STRICT solidifies the mark; WEIGHTED exempts the digit swaps and returns one to `admit` only when the cumulative guard trips), so this check stays live in the validator for that case and for any future split of the mark's pulse from `reduce_flashing`; the pin rests on the user's ratification, on this proof and on the cadence shared with the inspect card *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
506	
507	**Example:** (the floor) at `BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS` 128: `u` = 1 gives `ceil_div(128000, 3*128 - 60) = ceil_div(128000, 324) = 396` ms. At the range floor 120: `ceil_div(120000, 300) = 400` ms. At 180: 375 ms. (The retired edge unit `u` = 2 gave 485, 500 and 429 ms.) The Filter's PF-18 floor of 334 ms is `1000/3` for lying ticks alone and ignores the mark, which is why it is not the HUD's range floor.
508	
509	**Example (rates, a breach in progress, numerals falling every boundary)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: at `BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS` 128 and `HONEST_TICK_MS` 500, with `u` = 1. **WEIGHTED mode** (reduce flashing off, the mark pulsing): the mark counts `60/128 = 0.469`/s, the numerals (2.0/s) and the prompt show-starts are exempt, so the counted total is 0.469/s of 3 and a prompt waits for its 13-tick debounce alone. **STRICT mode** (reduce flashing on, the first-launch default): the mark is solid, so it adds 0; the numerals count 2.0/s, leaving 1.0/s for prompt show-starts (about one per second, bounded below by `PROMPT_MIN_CYCLE_TICKS`). The case that used to be the worst, a pulsing mark beside counted numerals (0.469 + 2.0 = 2.469/s, headroom 0.531/s; at the range floor 120, 0.5 + 2.0 = 2.5/s, headroom 0.5), now arises only when the cumulative guard trips, and the grid-skip rule and the window proof cover it.
510	
511	**Example (admission, no numerals; only show-starts are injected, with no hide events, so no pair completes in a window and no orphan hide arises: the hide cases are AC-HS-142)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: with plates hiding between show-starts a hide whose show-start has left the window is counted, D.2, and the admitted list below would shrink)*: show-start requests every 10 ticks from tick 0, filtered first by D.18 (`PROMPT_MIN_CYCLE_TICKS` 20), with a mark edge scheduled at tick 128, are admitted at 0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100 and 140 (the requests are filtered first by D.18, `PROMPT_MIN_CYCLE_TICKS` 20; `admit()` alone would also pass tick 10, whose window `(-50, 10]` holds only tick 0): the request at 120 is refused because the window ending at 128 would hold 80, 100, 120 and the edge (4); at 130 the window `(70, 130]` still holds 80, 100, 128 and the candidate; at 140 the window `(80, 140]` holds 100, 128 and the candidate (3). Long-run admitted rate `<= 3 - 0.469 = 2.53`/s.
512	
513	**Example (grid-skip, STRICT mode)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: the window is full (numerals 2.0/s plus a source-state hue cut, HSV-4, counted and never deferred, 1.0); a prompt show-start waits; the next grid boundary is skipped, the prompt is admitted in its slot, and the numeral shows the then-latest value one boundary later, so its lag is `<= 2 x 500` ms = 1000 ms. **Example (the bounds with their preconditions, STRICT mode)** *(re-review)*: the same window plus a second waiting prompt (a hue cut and two prompts): the first prompt is admitted at the skipped boundary's slot; the second would skip the next boundary too, but a boundary is never skipped twice in a row, so that boundary is drawn (numeral lag stays `<= 1000` ms, not the 1500 ms or more that unbounded skipping gave) and the second prompt waits for room, `<= MAX_DEFER_TICKS` 60 ticks, then is force-admitted and counted if the window is still full. The lamp glyph and scanner reading wait the same bound, so neither starves (AC-HS-141).
514	
515	**Example (Vertical Slice A overrun, stated so it is not a surprise):** with the reserve numeral lying at `T_tick` 400 ms (2.5 transitions/s), the O2 numeral honest (2.0/s) and one mark (0.469/s), STRICT mode counts 2.5 + 2.0 = 4.5/s `> 3` (the mark is solid there) and WEIGHTED mode counts the lying ticks (kept counted until the Filter adopts the same weighting) plus the mark, 2.5 + 0.469 = 2.969/s `<= 3` (margin 0.031/s), the honest numeral being exempt. The STRICT overrun is structural: the HUD cannot meet the ceiling by deferring its own events without starving the honest numeral, so it records `HUD_FLASH_OVERRUN` and raises the ask to the Filter; it never alters the Filter's schedule (CF-HS-10) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
516	
517	### D.3 reserve_seconds (HS-17; registered, HUD-owned)
518	
519	The reserve_seconds formula is defined as:
520	
521	`reserve_seconds = (displayed_pm * RESERVE_S + 999) div 1000`
522	
523	**Variables:**
524	
525	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
526	|---|---|---|---|---|
527	| `displayed_pm` | int permille | 0-1000 | `perceived(suit.reserve).displayed_pm` (the Filter's wrap), never `view.reserve_pm` | The reserve fraction as the player is shown it |
528	| `RESERVE_S` | int seconds | 90 (range 45-240) | Suit & Equipment (registry), cited | Seconds of breath at nominal draw |
529	| `reserve_seconds` | int seconds | 0..`RESERVE_S` | output | The numeral: three digit cells because `RESERVE_S` ranges to 240 |
530	
531	**Output Range:** 0 to `RESERVE_S`; the numeral is `0` only at exactly empty (the ceiling guarantees that a non-zero reserve never reads 0). It is the *latest* value at each `HONEST_TICK_MS` boundary. Nominal draw only: it is intentionally optimistic under a seam leak.
532	
533	**Example:** `RESERVE_S` 90: `displayed_pm` 1000 gives 90; 500 gives `(45000 + 999) div 1000 = 45`; 333 gives `(29970 + 999) div 1000 = 30` (equal to `RESERVE_WARN_S`); 12 gives `(1080 + 999) div 1000 = 2`; 11 gives 1; 1 gives 1; 0 gives 0. At nominal draw 1000/90 = 11.1 permille/s the displayed second changes about once per second, below the 3/s ceiling. With `RESERVE_S` 240 and 1000 permille the numeral is `240` (three cells). **Engraved warn notch** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: `warn_notch_px = (RESERVE_WARN_S * 16 + RESERVE_S - 1) div RESERVE_S` on the 16-px underlay track, 6 at `RESERVE_S` 90 and `RESERVE_WARN_S` 30 (the numeral reads 30 when the fill stands at the notch), 2 at `RESERVE_S` 240 and `RESERVE_WARN_S` 20; the fill is `(displayed_pm * 16 + 999) div 1000` px, so the fill is 6 px at the notch when `displayed_pm` is 333. The notch is frame (engraving), the fill is the reading.

535	### D.4 mark_phase (HS-23; registered, HUD-owned)
536	
537	The mark_phase formula is defined as:
538	
539	`phase_pm = ((T mod BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS) * 1000 + alpha_pm) div BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS ; ON iff phase_pm < MARK_DUTY_PM ; leading edge at T mod BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS == 0 ; override: an active mark is ON whatever phase_pm is while PAUSED_FROZEN, and under reduced motion or reduce-flashing`
540	
541	**Variables:**
542	
543	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
544	|---|---|---|---|---|
545	| `T` | int ticks | 0.. | kernel committed tick | Frozen under solo pause; the phase is not consulted while paused (HS-23 holds an active mark ON) |
546	| `alpha_pm` | int permille | 0-999 | `floor(tick_alpha * 1000)`, Pipeline | Sub-tick interpolation so the edge is drawn on the first render frame at or past the boundary |
547	| `BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS` | int ticks | 128 (range 120-180) | Emitter State (registry), cited | The period, by relation: `MARK_PERIOD_TICKS` is never a second value |
548	| `MARK_DUTY_PM` | int permille | 500 `[PH]`, range 400-600 | this GDD | Fraction of the period the mark is ON |
549	| `phase_pm` | int permille | 0-999 | output | Position in the period |
550	
551	**Output Range:** `phase_pm` in 0 to 999, monotone within a period and reset at the boundary; identical for all marks (no per-mark offset). One leading edge per period: `TICK_RATE / BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS` = 0.469/s at 128 (0.5 at 120, 0.333 at 180); both edges 0.94/s at 128. Worst-case latency for a mark that appears just past its duty is `(1000 - MARK_DUTY_PM)/1000 * BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS` = 64 ticks (1.07 s) at defaults, 76.8 ticks at duty 400. Reduced motion, reduce-flashing and `PAUSED_FROZEN`: ON while any mark is active, whatever `phase_pm` is (a pause cycle adds at most one leading edge, and a resume none: after a resume the mark is bridged ON until the next leading edge, HS-23). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
552	
553	**Example:** `T mod 128` = 63, `alpha_pm` 500: `(63000 + 500) div 128 = 496` so ON; `T mod 128` = 64, `alpha_pm` 0: `64000 div 128 = 500` so OFF; `T` = 300: `300 mod 128 = 44`, `44000 div 128 = 343` ON; `T` = 360: 104, 812 OFF; `T` = 384: 0, the leading edge, ON. The ON phase lasts 64 ticks (1.067 s) at defaults.
554	
555	### D.5 o2_dial_angle (HS-12, HS-13; registered, HUD-owned)
556	
557	The o2_dial_angle formula is defined as:
558	
559	`pm = clamp((displayed_value * 1000) div O2_DIAL_MAX_DKPA, 0, 1000) ; theta_cdeg = (STRIP_SWEEP_DEG * 100 * pm) div 1000 ; start_deg = 90 + STRIP_SWEEP_DEG div 2 (the left stop, measured counter-clockwise from +x; 180 at the default sweep) ; phi = start_deg - theta ; tip = (cx + round(L * cos(phi)), cy - round(L * sin(phi))) ; edge_theta(e) = (STRIP_SWEEP_DEG * e) div O2_DIAL_MAX_DKPA ; bbox_w = 2 * L, bbox_h = L * (1 + sin((STRIP_SWEEP_DEG - 180) / 2)) for a sweep of 180 or more` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the start angle and the bounding box are explicit, so a sweep other than 180 is computed rather than assumed; at 180 the tip is `(cx - round(L * cos(theta)), cy - round(L * sin(theta)))` as before)*
560	
561	**Variables:**
562	
563	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
564	|---|---|---|---|---|
565	| `displayed_value` | int dkPa | 0-999 (printed); dial clamps at the stop | `perceived(suit.o2).displayed_value` | The suit-sensed `p_o2` of the occupant's compartment (SE-30); equals `view.o2_pp_dkpa` on the honest path |
566	| `O2_DIAL_MAX_DKPA` | int dkPa | 300 `[PH]`, range 250-300 | this GDD; a calibration it supplies to the Filter (HS-26; no Filter consumer is named yet) | Dial travel; changing it rescales lie magnitude |
567	| `STRIP_SWEEP_DEG` | int degrees | 180 `[PH]`, range 120-240 | this GDD (named distinctly from Instruments' `DIAL_ARC_DEG`) | Sweep of the strip arc, measured from the left stop |
568	| `L` | int HUD px | at most 11 | art-director | Strip needle length (below the glide floor by construction, HS-29) |
569	| `cx`, `cy` | int HUD px | arc-cell coordinates | UX spec | Pivot position (bottom interior row) |
570	| `e` | int dkPa | the zone-edge value | read by name from the Graph (`HYPOXIA_PP`, 120-160 default 140; by name `O2_BAND_ANOXIC_PP` 100, `O2_BAND_THIN_PP` 180) | Never a literal in HUD data or source (lint) |
571	
572	**Source of the needle fraction:** the strip needle's `pm` is this formula's derivation from `displayed_value`; `Perceived.displayed_pm` for `suit.o2`, where the Filter publishes one, is asserted equal to it on the honest path (one source, so D.15's `displayed_pm` is this `pm`). **Output Range:** `theta` in 0 to `STRIP_SWEEP_DEG` degrees; the needle clamps at the stop and the numeral prints `min(displayed_value, 999)`. `1 permille = 0.3 dkPa < 0.5`, so `round(pm * 300 / 1000)` recovers every integer dkPa losslessly at range 300 (it would not above a 500-dkPa range).
573	
574	**Example:** a nominal room reads 210 dkPa: `pm = 210000 div 300 = 700`, `theta = 180 * 700/1000 = 126` degrees; with `L` 11 and the pivot at (12, 15) the tip is `(12 - round(11 * cos 126), 15 - round(11 * sin 126)) = (12 + 6, 15 - 9) = (18, 6)`. For 175 dkPa (the THIN fixture): `pm` 583, `theta` 105 degrees, tip `(12 + round(2.85), 15 - round(10.63)) = (15, 4)`. The Graph's registered edges (the HUD reads them by name), `O2_BAND_ANOXIC_PP` 100, `HYPOXIA_PP` 140 and `O2_BAND_THIN_PP` 180 dkPa, sit at `edge_theta` 60, 84 and 108 degrees; `HYPOXIA_PP` across its range 120-160 moves the middle one from 72 to 96 degrees. **Reserve branch** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; Resolved 2026-10-27 — re-review, G2, HS-12)*: while `breath_src` is RESERVE the strip's `pm` is `clamp(displayed_pm(suit.reserve), 0, 1000)` directly (permille of `RESERVE_S`, so no `O2_DIAL_MAX_DKPA` division and no dkPa literal), `theta_cdeg`, `phi`, `tip` and the frame index of D.15 follow unchanged, and the engraved reserve layer sits at `tank_theta = STRIP_SWEEP_DEG` (the full stop) and `warn_theta = (STRIP_SWEEP_DEG * warn_pm) div 1000`, with `warn_pm = (RESERVE_WARN_S * 1000 + RESERVE_S - 1) div RESERVE_S`. Example at `RESERVE_S` 90, `RESERVE_WARN_S` 30: a full reserve is `pm` 1000, `theta` 180 degrees, tip at the right stop, numeral `90`; 45 s is `pm` 500, 90 degrees, numeral `45`; the warn notch is `warn_pm` 334 at `warn_theta` 60 degrees (the numeral reads 30 at `displayed_pm` 333, which is 59.9 degrees, 0.2 degrees short of the notch, well inside one needle frame, so the needle stands on the notch when the numeral first reads 30, as D.3's panel notch does); at `RESERVE_S` 240 and `RESERVE_WARN_S` 20 `warn_pm` is 84 and `warn_theta` 15 degrees. The ambient branch's printed example (210 dkPa, 126 degrees) is the ROOM case and is unchanged. `breath_src` NONE or GASP uses the ambient branch (the strip then reads the room's `p_o2`, EC-HS-14).
575	
576	### D.6 hud_settle_response (HS-14; HUD-owned, presentation-only)
577	
578	The hud_settle_response formula (registry: `hud_settle_response`) is defined as below. It is the HUD's own suit-arc settle, named apart from In-World Instruments' `settle_response` (registry, source Instruments: `INSTR_SETTLE_ZETA` 0.7, omega 20, `INSTR_SETTLE_MS` 400, trigger `INSTR_SETTLE_JUMP_PM`), which it does not cite: the HUD's damping and settling time differ and only the shared second-order form and the 5 % overshoot / 250-400 ms bounds of art bible 7.3 are common. *(Renamed 2026-10-27, consistency pass, so the name has one owner.)* **Redefined 2026-10-27 (design review): the needle is a state, not a curve.** The earlier form was only the response to a single step from rest; it said nothing about a target that changes again mid-settle, which is the normal case in the anchor breach (the Graph steps `p_o2` every 6 ticks, about every 100 ms, against a 300 ms settle), and at its own defaults it was red against its own acceptance criterion (`|x - 1|` was 0.0248 at 300 ms). The response is now a critically damped, monotone, overshoot-free system advanced by an **exact per-frame propagator**; this section defines the pure function, and AC-HS-20 tests that function, not the drawn (quantised) needle. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
579	
580	`omega = K_SETTLE * 1000 / HUD_SETTLE_MS (rad/s) ; K_SETTLE = 5.834 ; state (p, v) in permille of dial travel and permille/s, target g ; e = p - g ; advance(dt): B = v + omega * e ; E = exp(-omega * dt) ; e' = (e + B * dt) * E ; v' = (v - omega * B * dt) * E ; p' = g + e' ; retarget(g_new): g := g_new, p and v unchanged ; rest: if |e'| < REST_PM and |v'| < REST_V then p := g, v := 0 ; sub-frame: if at rest and |g_new - p| < FRAME_PM then g := g_new and p, v are unchanged (no settle starts; the deltas accumulate in e = p - g and the settle starts the first time |e| >= FRAME_PM) ; reduced motion: p := g, v := 0 on every retarget` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
581	
582	`K_SETTLE` is the root of `(1 + x) * exp(-x) = 0.02` (5.8339), the 2 % settle of a critically damped step, so the step response from rest `e(t) = e0 * (1 + omega * t) * exp(-omega * t)` is **exactly 2 % at `t = HUD_SETTLE_MS`** (0.019999 at the default) and is monotone with no overshoot. `REST_PM` (1) and `REST_V` (10 permille/s) are numeric hygiene so the exponential tail ends; they are not knobs. `FRAME_PM` is one needle frame step, `1000 / (N_frames - 1)` (D.15). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
583	
584	**Properties the function guarantees (each is an acceptance criterion).** (P1) *Semigroup:* `advance(a)` then `advance(b)` equals `advance(a + b)` to float precision, so three 16.7 ms steps and one 50 ms step agree and the clamp `HUD_DT_CLAMP_MS` only bounds a hitch. (P2) *Continuity:* a retarget changes neither `p` nor `v`; the needle position is continuous at every retarget. (P3) *No backward motion:* between retargets `B' = -omega * B`, and a retarget by `delta` adds `omega * delta` to `B`, so for any sequence of retargets in one direction `B` keeps the sign of `e`, the needle never crosses its target and never moves against the direction of travel; only a retarget that reverses direction can cause one turn-around. (P4) *Bounded lag under a ramp:* a target moving at constant rate `r` (permille/s) is followed at a steady lag of `2 * r / omega`, plus at most one retarget step for a staircase. (P5) *Below one needle frame a change does not start a settle* (the sub-frame rule), **but sub-frame changes accumulate** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the earlier form set `p := g_new` on every sub-frame retarget, so on the reference ramp of -12 dkPa/s, 4 permille per Graph step against a `FRAME_PM` of 29.4, the needle stepped with the target and the settle never engaged, which contradicted the steady-lag example below)*: the target moves, `p` waits, and when 8 such steps (32 permille) are owed the settle starts from `p` and follows the ramp at the steady lag of P4. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
585	
586	**Fallback if the art-director insists on a visible overshoot:** use the underdamped form with `zeta >= 0.70` and `omega_n = ln(50 / sqrt(1 - zeta^2)) / (zeta * Ts)`, re-derive the peak (`pi / omega_d`, 0.217 s at `zeta` 0.70 and 300 ms; overshoot 4.6 %), and restore a `HUD_SETTLE_ZETA` knob, the peak assertions and registry entry. It is not adopted: art bible 7.3's 5 % is a ceiling, and the overshoot is 0.2-0.4 px, which never renders. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
587	
588	**Variables:**
589	
590	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
591	|---|---|---|---|---|
592	| `dt` | real seconds | 0..`HUD_DT_CLAMP_MS` | `present_time` step, clamped to `HUD_DT_CLAMP_MS`; no integrator divides by it | Frozen under pause (`dt` = 0); never process time. The propagator is exact for any `dt`, so the frame rate never changes the result |
593	| `HUD_SETTLE_MS` | int ms | 300 `[PH]`, range 250-400 | this GDD; art bible 7.3 bounds it | The 2 % settling time of a step from rest, exactly (named to avoid Instruments' own `INSTR_SETTLE_MS`, CF-HS-20) |
594	| `K_SETTLE` | real | 5.834 (derived constant, not a knob) | root of `(1 + x) * exp(-x) = 0.02` | Converts the settling time to `omega`; `HUD_SETTLE_ZETA` is retired |
595	| `p`, `v`, `g`, `e` | real | `p`, `g` in 0-1000 permille of dial travel; `v` in permille/s | the needle state, the target (`displayed_pm`, or D.5's `pm`), `e = p - g` | The state is held per needle; a retarget replaces `g` only |
596	| `FRAME_PM` | real permille | 1000 / (`N_frames` - 1): 29.4 at `L` 11, 20 at `L` 16, 13.3 at `L` 24 (180 degrees) | D.15 | One needle frame step; the sub-frame rule's threshold |
597	| `REST_PM`, `REST_V` | real | 1 permille; 10 permille/s | this GDD (numeric hygiene) | Ends the exponential tail |
598	
599	**Output Range:** `p` in 0-1000, clamped to the dial stops; for a one-direction run of retargets `p` is monotone and never passes `g`; the drawn needle is then quantised to whole HUD px and frame (D.15). Reduced motion: `p = g` on the retarget (a step). A non-HONEST record never settles (HS-28). Paused: `dt` = 0, no change. Restore: `p = g`, `v = 0` (RESTORE_FRAME). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
600	
601	**Example:** `HUD_SETTLE_MS` 300: `omega = 5.834 / 0.3 = 19.45` rad/s. A step from rest of 200 permille (36 degrees: O2 falling 210 to 150 dkPa at 300 dkPa travel and 180 degrees): `e` after 0.1 s is `200 * (1 + 1.945) * exp(-1.945) = 84.2` permille (42.1 %), after 0.2 s 20.0 (10.0 %), after 0.3 s 4.0 (2.0 %), and at frame 19 (316.7 ms) 3.0 (1.5 %): **the 2 % criterion holds at the settle time and at every later frame**. Ramp: `p_o2` falling 12 dkPa/s is `r` = 40 permille/s, the steady lag is `2 * 40 / 19.45 = 4.1` permille (about 1.2 dkPa, 0.74 degrees, 0.14 px at the strip's 11-px needle); the needle never moves backward. Mid-settle retarget: at `t` = 0.1 s into the step above (`e` 84.2 permille, `v` about -1,080 permille/s) the target drops another 4 permille (one Graph step): `p` and `v` are unchanged at that instant, `e` becomes 88.2 and the response continues from there, so there is no restart, no kink in position and no second 300 ms. Two 16.7 ms steps then one 16.7 ms step equal one 50 ms step to float precision. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
602	
603	### D.7 nonground_count (HS-56; registered, HUD-owned)
604	
605	The nonground_count formula is defined as:
606	
607	`nonground_count = #{ (x, y) in [0, 640) x [0, 360) : colour(x * H + H div 2, y * H + H div 2) is neither GROUND (#1C2128) nor SENTINEL } ; require nonground_count <= HUD_NONGROUND_PX_MAX = (HUD_NONGROUND_PCT_X10 * 640 * 360) div 1000`
608	
609	**Variables:**
610	
611	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
612	|---|---|---|---|---|
613	| `colour(px)` | sRGB | the captured layer | screenshot with the world container hidden and the root clear colour set to the SENTINEL (for example `#FF00FF`) | Transparent HUD pixels show the clear colour, not alpha, so the sentinel is how "transparent" is counted |
614	| `H` | int | `H_default` (capture at 3 on 1080p so the canvas is exactly 640 x 360) | Pipeline | Block-centre sampling at integer `H` |
615	| `HUD_NONGROUND_PCT_X10` | int | 10 (range 10-15), i.e. 1.0 %-1.5 % | this GDD `[PH]` | The art bible's "about 1 %, tunable" (ab:754) as a measurable cap |
616	| `HUD_NONGROUND_PX_MAX` | int HUD px | 2304 (range 2304-3456) | derived | The budget |
617	
618	**Output Range:** 0 to 230,400; measured **at rest** only (all readings OK, no prompt, mark, notice, first-frame line or inspect card; the card is outside the measurement, iw:327). A scan is a tool-time cost (230,400 samples), dev only.

905	## Edge Cases
906	
907	Ids are `EC-HS-n`. Each case states the exact outcome, never "handle gracefully". Cases the rulings overrode in the specialists' lists are not repeated: the clamped-plate fallback (HS-39 draws no plate instead), a centre-low first-frame line and a non-deferrable notice (HS-46 and HS-47 place both at the panel's edge, the notice at the third deferral priority), and the retired alpha-ramp gleam and `NUMERAL_MIN_HOLD_TICKS` (replaced by lit-length and `HONEST_TICK_MS`).
908	
909	### Scale, layout and display
910	
911	- **If `H` changes while a channel is running**: the layout is recomputed on the next render frame by the pure `HudLayout` function; the plate and bar re-quantise to the new `H`; the bar does not reset, its `fill_px` is recomputed from `channel_view.progress_pm`; nothing is read from or written to the simulation. The change is a cut, never a tween (SCALE_CHANGE state). (EC-HS-1)
912	- **If the zoom ladder steps from `k` 3 to 1 or to `k_auto + 2` mid-channel and the anchor now projects outside the picture rect**: the plate and the bar, which rides the plate, hide on the next render frame and are never clamped to the frame edge; when the anchor returns they reappear without a debounce reset, and the bar's fill is recomputed from `progress_pm`; the simulation's channel is unaffected. This is distinct from losing `lit` (EC-HS-32), where the plate hides but the bar stays. Zoom changes plate position by re-projection only; plate and bar sizes are HUD px and do not change. (EC-HS-2)
913	- **If a settings value or a window size produces a `(picture, H)` pair for which `fit` is false**: `HudLayout` returns a defect flag (an assertion in debug, the counter `hud_layout_overlap` in release) and the pipeline root falls back to the layout at `H_default` (always offered; there may be no previous layout after a resize or at first mount); the settings offer only `offered(P_w, P_h)` (D.8). At MVP the offered steps are the Pipeline's PR-12 option (a), computed per panel arrangement (D.8): a 1280 x 720 window offers `H` 3 and 4 under COLUMN and `H` 3 only under ROW (`H` 4 gives 102 HUD px per side against the ROW panel's 144; `H` 5 and 6 give 73 and 53 against COLUMN's 74). The no-overlap rule is binding (HS-54). (EC-HS-3) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
914	- **If the display is the Steam Deck (1280 x 800, `H` 3 over a `k` 2 world) under `keep`** (the picture mode pinned for every Deck figure here; `expand` is the Pipeline's post-spike ideal and would only add canvas height, 266.67 HUD px): the canvas is 426.67 x 240 HUD px *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; every rectangle is floored to a whole HUD px, the sub-`H` remainder (`extra_x` 2 screen px at `H` 3) is split by `anchor_snap`, right and bottom slack is at most 1 HUD px, and nine-slice borders sit on whole HUD px, so no half-pixel border appears; the strip is about 15 % of the width, the accepted platform overage (HS-15). Behaviour of `gui_snap_controls_to_pixels` here is NOT SOURCEABLE until the spike (HS-9). (EC-HS-4)
915	- **If the picture is wider than 16:9 (an ultrawide)**: the strip stays centred on the picture rect, the panel and rail anchor to its edges inside the 5 % margin, and no element stretches or reflows, because layout is a pure function of `(picture rect, H)` (HS-51); more canvas width only adds slack to `bottom_row_fit`. The Pipeline owns the rect. (EC-HS-5)
916	- **If a `Control` is parented under the world `SubViewport`**: the scene-tree lint fails the build (Pipeline lint (b)); it is a build gate, not a runtime check, because in a release build the node would receive world light, glow and the Filter. (EC-HS-6)
917	- **If the prompt anchor is on screen but no placement satisfies the chest keep-out `PROMPT_KEEPOUT_PX` 16 and the `PROMPT_EDGE_MARGIN_PX` 4 margin after Interaction's AD-5 side order and the world-px fallback offset**: the plate is not drawn (as if off screen), never clamped over the chest; counter `UI_PLACEMENT_WITHHELD`. A plate over the chest point would mask the beam origin, which is the pointer. (EC-HS-7)
918	- **If a candidate plate position would overlap the strip, panel or rail rectangles**: the plate is moved to the next AD-5 side or withheld; it is never drawn over a reading. The three rectangles are an exclusion region. (EC-HS-8)
919	
920	### Clocks, pause and time
921	
922	- **If the kernel is paused (solo) while a mark is mid-pulse**: `T` stops, and every active mark is held ON solid, undimmed, from the first paused frame (HS-23; CF-HS-13 resolved by the art-director's alternative): a frozen OFF outline can no longer read as safe beside a CRITICAL reading. An inactive slot stays empty. On resume the mark follows the unchanged `T`; the pause cycle costs at most one mark leading edge (the arbiter counts it, never delays it). Layer 3 (the Chart Table) stays live on process time over the HUD. (EC-HS-9)
923	- **If the game resumes after a 10 s pause, a window-focus loss or a hitch**: the first post-resume time step fed to any presentation timer is clamped to `HUD_DT_CLAMP_MS` 50; no latch, debounce, settle or tick fires from the gap; a forced discrete rebuild runs (HS-7); the honest grid is re-armed. No integrator divides by the time step. (EC-HS-10)
924	- **If the render rate is 30 fps and a mark edge falls between render frames**: the edge is drawn on the first render frame whose `(T, tick_alpha)` is at or past the boundary (at most 33.3 ms skew against the audio edge) and counted once; there is no double edge. If a hitch skips a whole `BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS` period the mark shows the phase of the current `(T, alpha_pm)` with no catch-up pulses. (EC-HS-11)
925	- **If `T` is read before the first committed tick (boot)**: the surface state is UNMOUNTED, nothing is drawn, `view()` is not read, the mark phase is 0 and no mark exists (no rung). The HUD draws the last committed state; none means nothing. (EC-HS-12)

927	### Readings: zero, maximum and out of range

929	- **If `suit.o2` `displayed_value` exceeds `O2_DIAL_MAX_DKPA` (an enriched compartment)**: the needle clamps at the right stop (`pm` 1000), the numeral prints `min(displayed_value, 999)`, and nothing spills into the mark slot. The fixed three-column field cannot grow. (EC-HS-13)

(EC-HS-14) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
931	- **If `breath_src` changes between ROOM and RESERVE faster than the player can read it (a threshold flicker, for example a hatch cycling)**: the swap of HS-12 (3) is drawn on each frame that reads a new enum value and is one counted source-state event per change, never deferred; the Suit publishes `breath_src_change_seq` and its own rung hold, so the HUD adds no debounce of its own; if repeated swaps would exceed `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` the overrun is recorded as `HUD_FLASH_OVERRUN` and nothing else changes (it is a published source state, like a hue cut). Both honest numerals are armed on each swap, so no numeral boundary lands within the same grid cell. (EC-HS-56) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
932	- **If `RESERVE_S` is tuned to 240**: the reserve numeral uses all three digit cells at every `H` (`240` at full), the panel row is authored for three digits, and `reserve_seconds` is `0` only at exactly empty. (EC-HS-15)
933	- **If the reserve is refilled (a top-up, MVP-live: `top_up` is an MVP verb, user ruling X5)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: the numeral counts upward in whole steps at the honest grid, never tweened; a boundary at which no displayed digit changed is not a luminance event; the dial-less reserve has no needle to settle. (EC-HS-16)
934	- **If `perceived(SUIT_KEY(k), PlayerId)` returns no record for a key not yet registered**: that reading's plate draws with a blank numeral and the arc at rest, `HUD_READ_MISSING` is counted, and the HUD never falls back to `view()`'s reading fields. (EC-HS-17)
935	- **If a stub Filter returns `leak_amplitude_pm` below 0 or above 1000, or `displayed_pm` out of range**: the HUD clamps to range and counts `hud_perceived_oob`; the record is a request and the Filter's own honest fallback is the owner's. (EC-HS-18)
936	- **If `CELL_ENABLED` is 0** (a data edge case; the cell is on at MVP, user ruling X5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: the charge cell is an empty slot, with no "disabled" art and no mark; `toggle_beam` still has its keycap only when a cell exists (the lamp switch lives on the charge row). (EC-HS-19)
937	- **If the Suit retunes `TL_STRAINED`, `TL_CRITICAL` or `TL_MAX`, or the published edge list is not the four inner edges of SE-29**: the notches move with the Suit's published edges (D.14); the HUD never keeps a literal edge and never invents one; a build whose edge read is missing or not strictly increasing in 0-1000 draws no notch ticks, counts `hud_perceived_oob` and fails the data-load lint. The earlier "Suit has not yet published" case is closed: SE-29 publishes the axis and the edges. (EC-HS-20) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
938	- **If the O2 numeral and the reserve numeral both change at one grid boundary**: they are one luminance event, not two (a boundary is one event however many digits change); both show the latest values. (EC-HS-21)
939	
940	### The warning mark
941	
942	- **If several axes are CRITICAL at once (up to six marks: strip, reserve cell, warmth, integrity, charge and the ship-alarm slot; the strip and reserve marks coexist while `breath_src` is `RESERVE`, HS-22)**: all marks share one phase (no per-mark offset), the leading edge is one event in `hud_flash_budget`, and the worst-case Alarm Red area is six marks of 16 x 16 (1,536 px at 256 each), which the visual criterion measures; at rest it is zero. (EC-HS-22) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
943	- **If a rung falls from CRITICAL to a lower rung mid-pulse**: the mark hides on that render frame (hide is never deferred); the slot returns to empty, not to the OFF outline. (EC-HS-23)
944	- **If the seat is DOWNED**: the readings keep updating, the lamp stays lit, the marks persist and pulse (or stay solid, HS-23), there is no banner and no tint, and the solo "give up and reload" action (user ruling D7) is the Controller's command, drawn on the HUD only as the DOWNED-only `give_up` confirm plate (`hud_give_up_plate`, HS-42(b)): visible from the first DOWNED frame with the bar at 0, bar = `confirm_view.hold_pm`, gone on the first frame `confirm_view.give_up_live` is false; the plate carries no text beyond its verb, no banner, no tint *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; walk-only is surfaced by the breath and warmth readings *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. If the seat is restored into DEAD, no mark is drawn. (EC-HS-24)
945	- **If `give_up_live` drops and rises again within `PROMPT_MIN_CYCLE_TICKS` (20) ticks of the plate's last show-start**: the hide is immediate; the re-show waits until `since_last_show >= 20` (so at most 3 show-starts per second, `floor(60 / 20)`); the Controller still accepts a press in the gap and the plate catches up with the live `hold_pm`. Example: show at T = 100, `give_up_live` false at T = 105, true at T = 110 -> plate re-shown at T = 120. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* (EC-HS-57)
946	- **If `reduced_motion` is on**: the needle settle becomes a one-frame step (`p = g`), the cosmetic drain snaps to 0, glide slows by `RM_GLIDE_SCALE` but keeps drift and wander, the lying tick never falls below `LIE_TICK_MS`, and the mark holds ON solid (HR-8; settled by user ruling D91 (v): reduced motion still solidifies the mark, because a pulse is also a flash effect) with the Adaptive Audio sound carrying the alarm. **If `reduce_flashing` is on** (its first-launch default, user ruling D79): the mark holds ON solid, the arbiter runs in STRICT mode (every event of HS-47 counts, no area exemption), and nothing else changes: the settle, glide and drain are untouched, and the honest grid stays on its pinned cadence. The two settings are separate by what they change; the earlier table row said `reduce_flashing` leaves "no luminance events beyond show-starts", which this case contradicted. Under reduced motion a deaf player has the solid `suit.alarm` mark as the HUD ship-alarm cue (CF-HS-4, closed by user ruling D89). (EC-HS-25) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
947	- **If a Vertical Slice A lying suit reading and its rung mark disagree**: the rung mark follows the reading's class (HS-30), so it may be absent beside a lying reading; the ship-alarm mark, if drawn, never follows a lie. No Acceptance Criterion asserts it (CF-HS-19); the MVP rule stands: the Suit's rung drives the mark, the HUD never computes CRITICAL from `displayed_value`. (EC-HS-26)
948	
949	### The flash arbiter
950	
951	- **If a prompt show-start is waiting and the window is full** (STRICT mode, or an unexempt plate in WEIGHTED mode, D.2): with the honest grid running, the next grid boundary is skipped, the prompt is admitted in its slot, and the numeral shows the then-latest value one boundary later (lag at most `2 x HONEST_TICK_MS`, unconditionally: a boundary is never skipped twice in a row). The prompt waits at most one grid cell when at most one other counted event is in the window, otherwise at most `MAX_DEFER_TICKS` 60 ticks and is then force-admitted and counted. Hides and mark edges are never deferred. (EC-HS-27) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
952	- **If the lamp is toggled ten times in one second**: the world beam is never debounced (the cone is the truth); the charge-row glyph change is a **state-display draw** (HS-47 class A): the shared limiter admits at most one draw per `GLYPH_STATE_LATCH_TICKS` 20 across the whole class (so the glyph, the tool bracket, the glowstick count and the TAP relabel share three draws a second), each draw shows the latest state (ten toggles, an even number, end on the starting state and draw at most the net change), and a pending draw is force-admitted at `MAX_DEFER_TICKS` 60; the glyph may therefore lag the beam by up to 0.333 s in the common case and 1 s at the bound, and the HUD cannot flash faster than 3/s through the class. (EC-HS-28) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
953	- **If a lie starts while an honest latch is armed on the same numeral**: the Filter's record wins; the honest latch state is dropped on the first non-HONEST `motion_mode`; on RETURN to HONEST the grid restarts armed, with no immediate change allowed for one grid cell. (EC-HS-29)
954	- **If the sum of non-deferrable events (Vertical Slice A lying ticks plus marks) already exceeds `FLASH_MAX_PER_S`**: the HUD records `HUD_FLASH_OVERRUN`, defers every deferrable event it can, changes nothing in the Filter's schedule, and the ask to the Filter and accessibility-specialist stands (CF-HS-10). It is unreachable at MVP. (EC-HS-30)
955	
956	### Prompts, the bar and input
957	
958	- **If focus changes every 12 ticks along a corridor**: `PROMPT_SHOW_DEBOUNCE_TICKS` 13 and `PROMPT_MIN_CYCLE_TICKS` 20 together mean a plate that has not been stable for 13 ticks never shows (at the earlier 9 ticks a plate stable for 9 and then replaced at 12 popped for 50 ms, so the claim was false at the defaults), no plate shows even for one frame under the 12-tick churn, and no more than three plates start per second; hides are immediate. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* This is the guarantee Interaction's AC-IA-72 assigns to this GDD. (EC-HS-31)
959	- **If the subject stops being lit mid-channel**: the plate hides the same render frame `prompt_state` goes HIDDEN, but the bar stays until the simulation's abort (at most 5 dark ticks), then plays the one ABORT frame set. The HUD never queries `lit`. (EC-HS-32)
960	- **If a world abort and the player's release land close together**: the drain is keyed off Interaction's `channel_view.ended_by` (registry `ended_by`), not the Adapter's release read: `PLAYER_CANCEL` draws the drain, `WORLD` draws the snap-plus-notch. `ended_by` is written with the terminal state, so a world abort inside tick t's hook that lands before the Adapter's `cancel_channel` (applied as `IA_CANCEL_NOOP` at t+1) reads `WORLD` and draws the snap-plus-notch; the one-tick race does not arise. (EC-HS-33)
961	- **If a press is rejected immediately**: any pre-drawn ACK (keycap drop, empty track) is withdrawn within one render frame; nothing shakes, flashes, reddens or explains; the result is identical for every rejection reason; the restored keycap is held Graphite-lit for `BAR_REJECT_HOLD_TICKS` (at most one reject presentation per seat per `PROMPT_MIN_CYCLE_TICKS`) so a rejected press on a shown plate leaves a perceivable trace, and a reject with no plate shown draws nothing. (EC-HS-34) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
962	- **If the ACK pre-play is drawn and no CONFIRMED arrives within `PREPLAY_MAX_TICKS` 2**: the pre-play is withdrawn; a late CONFIRMED redraws the track at fill 0 and continues from `progress_pm`. (EC-HS-35)
963	- **If the input device switches while a channel or hold is non-IDLE**: the glyph set is latched and swaps at the next prompt show after `DEVICE_SWITCH_HYSTERESIS` (cited by name); the bar does not reset; the swap redraws only the keycap region. (EC-HS-36)
964	- **If the player rebinds `interact` to a key outside the closed token set**: the keycap is the wide `?` token, `hud_unmapped_key_glyph` is counted, and the prompt plate's width budget already reserves the wide case so nothing reflows. (EC-HS-37)
965	- **If a `tr()` key is missing, or a translated string exceeds the +40 % pseudo-locale budget**: a missing key renders the key and counts `UI_MISSING_KEY`; an over-long string wraps to a second line at `PROMPT_PLATE_MAX_W_PX` 72 and, if two lines still overflow, the plate grows taller and `hud_plate_overflow` is counted; the face is never shrunk or truncated (grow, not clip: orchestrator ruling, see HS-49). (EC-HS-38)
966	- **If a module is carried and the focused world target is not in the closed carry set**: no prompt is drawn for it; the only prompts are `G . Drop`, `verb_install` at a compatible hardpoint, the pod-console hop plate and the door face's V4 plate *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. (EC-HS-39)
967	- **If the player holds hold-to-confirm while the game is soloed-paused**: gameplay input is not accepted in the paused context, so `b` and `present_time` cannot diverge in solo; in a co-op OVERLAY pause the kernel runs and `present_time` runs. (EC-HS-40)
968	- **If the player spams the interact key to flash plates**: the plate cycle is bounded by `PROMPT_MIN_CYCLE_TICKS` (at most 3 show-starts per second) and by the arbiter; a held focus shows once and stays. The accepted-press ACK plus force-admitted show-start is rate-gated to one per `PROMPT_MIN_CYCLE_TICKS` per seat, is counted, never deferred, and **may overrun a full window**; the overrun is recorded as `HUD_FLASH_OVERRUN`. **Nothing the player does can raise the HUD above `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` through a deferrable or state-display event** (the shared limiter of HS-47 class A coalesces the tool bracket, the glowstick count, the lamp glyph and the TAP relabel); the acknowledgement cues of class B are the stated exception and are counted. (EC-HS-41) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
969	
970	### Save, restore and life state
971	
972	- **If the first `RUNNING` frame follows a restore**: readings are drawn directly at the restored values (no settle, no abort frame, no break-notch), every presentation-local counter is cleared (debounce, grid, bar fill and drain, tick phases, flash history, device latch), the mark draws ON at once if the live phase is inside its duty (no start artefact), and `restore_reason` is read as a request that never alters hallucination content from `DEATH_STUB` (it keys only the one record line of HS-46, shown for `UI7_DWELL_S`). (EC-HS-42) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
973	- **If the seat is restored into DEAD, or dies**: the readings freeze at the last drawn values; there is no death screen, score, text or fade; no mark is drawn after a restore into DEAD; the last light and the cryo-bay lamp are world beats. (EC-HS-43)
974	- **If `save_status` flips FAILED, WRITTEN and FAILED within one frame**: the notice follows the last committed value; the failure count is Save/Load's; the notice has no animation, so it adds no luminance event beyond its show-start. (EC-HS-44)
975	- **If the first-frame line and the failed-write notice are shown together**: both stack at the suit panel's edge (the line above the notice slot), each is a deferrable show-start; neither enters the bottom-centre band; the line dwells `UI7_DWELL_S` 8 on `present_time` then cuts, the notice persists until `WRITTEN`. (EC-HS-45)
976	- **If the Chart Table has already shown the corrupt-ring line under Continue**: the HUD shows nothing for it. (EC-HS-46)
977	- **If an `ALL`-coalesced dirty notification arrives during a loading hitch (more than `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256 keys)**: a full discrete rebuild runs; no dirty bookkeeping survives; readings are pulled fresh every frame regardless. (EC-HS-47)
978	- **If the pod hop (`TRANSIT_HOLD`) is in progress**: the HUD's layout is unchanged and statuses run in the pod (user ruling D60), so the readings keep updating from `perceived` (the dial settles and the numerals tick on the grid as in RUNNING), remain lie-capable, and a prompt shows only if a lit plate exists; if the seat dies in the pod the HUD enters DEAD like anywhere else and the restore follows HS-53. (EC-HS-48) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
979	
980	### Hallucination interplay
981	
982	- **If the scanner slot receives a lying record (Vertical Slice A) while no scanner is equipped**: the slot is not drawn and no record is requested; the gleam draws only while its host reading draws. (EC-HS-49)
983	- **If a `frame_override` names an atlas region the HUD's table lacks**: the reading draws its honest frame and `hud_unknown_override` is counted (the Filter's own honest-fallback rule). (EC-HS-50)
984	- **If the honest O2 numeral and a lying wall gauge disagree at MVP-equivalent fixtures**: the HUD draws `perceived(suit.o2).displayed_value`, which equals the compartment's `p_o2`; that disagreement is the designed second-instrument beat, not a defect, and the HUD never flags which one is wrong. (EC-HS-51)
985	- **If a readout is lie-capable but `READING_LIE_STAGE` is "never" (all keys at MVP) and `SCANNER_LIE_STAGE` is never**: the slots are inert; a stub Filter drives them only in tests; a build with a non-"never" value is a Vertical Slice A build and out of this GDD's MVP scope. (EC-HS-52)
986	- **If the player reads the reserve numeral during a seam leak**: the numeral is nominal-draw and intentionally optimistic; the true time left is shorter; the seam jet and the hiss are the falsifier. This is documented, not a defect, provided the Suit's cue-margin check holds (HS-17, OQ-HS-60); whether players read it as a "lie" is a playtest question (OQ-HS-58). (EC-HS-53)
987	
988	### Co-op hooks (Vertical Slice B, reserved)
989	
990	- **If a co-op OVERLAY panel covers the bottom-right hand rail**: the HUD is correct; no rule depends on the rail being visible and nothing is drawn elsewhere to compensate. (EC-HS-54)
991	- **If more than one seat exists**: only the local seat's `perceived`, `view`, `focus_view` and `channel_view` are drawn; addressing is by PlayerId, never `peer_id`; another seat's bar is never drawn; the `crew_strip`, `chat`, `caption` and `own_identity` anchors draw nothing at MVP. (EC-HS-55)

1711	## Acceptance Criteria

The two are **offset** (for example AC-HS-13 verifies HS-11), so a story must cite the **rule id**, never the AC number alone. Tags written `(auto)` in the first draft of a pixel or draw-call criterion are corrected to this one. **(lint)** a static or scene-tree scan of source, data, scenes or atlas names. **(review)** a reviewer reads text or data and records a line in the evidence file. **(manual)** a launched build observed by a person, with a **retained screenshot in `production/qa/evidence/`** (a parse check is not a run; a manual criterion is not closed until its screenshot is on disk). **(manual+auto)** the model is asserted headlessly and the look is proved by a retained screenshot; use it wherever the observable is visual. **(auto, provisional)** written against the HUD's proposed Adapter or Suit read and re-based when the owner answers the ASK. **(spike)** a measured prototype whose result is recorded in Open Questions with PASS or FAIL and a named fallback; a spike does not gate a story. **MVP** = live at MVP; **RESERVED** = specified and built, dormant until Vertical Slice A or B (driven by a stub Filter or stub seat in tests). "THIN fixture" = a compartment with `p_o2` inside the THIN band and an honest suit. **No criterion asserts what a Vertical Slice A lying reading does to its warning mark, in either direction** (CF-HS-19, CF-HS-15).

1920	- **Counter semantics** for `UI_MISSING_KEY` (once per distinct key per plate show) are a ruling made here and should be confirmed by the UX spec.
