Marked "*(Amended 2026-10-28 — ...)*".
14	
15	## Summary
16	
17	The HUD & Suit Layer is the player's own screen: a few small opaque plates at the edges of the picture that show what the suit knows about its wearer (the air in the room, the reserve breath, the suit's soundness, warmth and lamp charge), what the hands hold, and, only over a lit object, one key and one verb with a thin bar that fills while a long job runs. It exists because the suit, the interaction rules and the Perception Filter are all headless, and because the game's governing rule (the HUD is a suit, the ship is an instrument) needs one owner so that no other system invents its own readouts. It draws, decides nothing, and keeps two registers apart: a frame that never lies, and six readings that can lie only once Vertical Slice A switches the Filter on.
18	
19	> **Quick reference** — Layer: Presentation · Priority: MVP · Key deps: Pixel-Perfect Render Pipeline & Camera, Suit & Equipment, Perception Filter, Player Controller & Input (the four index dependencies, all Hard); Interaction System (Hard, prompts and bar; missing from the index row, reported to the producer, never edited here); Command & Simulation Layer (Hard, `PRESENTATION` subscription); Save/Load & Versioned Format (Soft, `save_status` only)
20	
21	## Overview
22	
23	HUD & Suit Layer is the presentation system that owns **layer 2** of the render pipeline: the player's own screen. In one sentence, it is a scene-tree-side, `PRESENTATION`-class drawing system in the root viewport that, every render frame, draws what five upstream systems publish about the local seat — the critical strip (the breath dial: the ambient O2 arc and numeral, or the reserve's while the suit breathes from it, HS-12), the suit panel (reserve, integrity, warmth, charge and the lamp switch), the hand rail (three tools, the glowstick count, the carried module, the scanner reading slot), the warning marks, the interaction prompt plate with its linear channel bar, the failed-write notice and the first-frame ship-log line — and owns the Godot `Theme`, the shared component set and the lying-reading drawing slots (gleam, motion signature, sound request) that the Perception Filter parameterises. The rail holds three tools at MVP in a four-slot geometry (the suppressant leaves the MVP kit, X6), the warning marks are six slots (five suit rungs and the one-bit ship alarm, D89), and the first-frame line also fires once after a death restore (D15). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* It creates **no simulation state**: no block, hook, command, mutator, reading key, RNG stream or `INPUT_SURFACE`. Everything it decides is *how* a value looks; every *when* — a rung and its hold, whether a prompt exists, how long a bar is, whether a reading lies, how many writes failed — is cited from the system that owns it.
24	
25	**How the player meets it.** Not as a menu and not as a dashboard but as **a visor**: a few small opaque plates at the edges of the picture that never move, scale, tint or flash, with a few thin readings moving inside them. At the bottom centre sits a strip with a dial arc and a three-digit number — the suit's own reading of the air in the compartment the wearer stands in, and, once the suit is breathing its reserve, the seconds of reserve left (HS-12). At the bottom left sits a small panel for the things the suit carries about itself: how many seconds of reserve breath remain, how sound the suit is, how warm, how much charge the chest lamp has and whether it is switched on. At the bottom right sits the hand rail: the three tools, how many glowsticks are left, and what is held in the hands. Over a lit object in the world, and only there, a small plate shows one key and one verb; when the player commits to a long job, that plate grows a thin linear bar that fills one whole pixel at a time. Once in a rare while a small red-and-white mark appears beside a reading (or, for a ship alarm, in its own slot on the panel), pulsing in step with the ship's beacon (held solid at the first-launch default, HS-23). There is nothing else: no minimap, no objective, no room name, no health bar, no sanity or Attention indicator under any setting. The numbers are a **second opinion** — the body (breath, a click at the collar, a fogging visor) and the room (a leaking pipe, a frosted wall) speak first. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
26	
27	**What the game loses without it.** Suit & Equipment is headless: it "has no screen of its own", and its five readings, its tool roster and its counts reach no eye. Interaction is headless: it draws none of its prompts or its bar. The concept's single hypothesis — a 30-minute solo boarding-then-breach session that is tense and absorbing — needs the player to read their own body and to be told what a press will do. Pillar 4 loses its only cheap falsifier at MVP: the honest `suit.o2` numeral is the "second instrument" that exposes a lying wall gauge, and it is the HUD that shows it. And the art bible's governing rule — *the HUD is a suit, the ship is an instrument* — has no owner, so every other presentation system would invent its own readouts.
28	
29	**Two registers, kept apart (HS-3).** The **frame register** — plates, bezels, rivets, keycaps, labels, prompts, the channel bar, rail glyphs and counts, the failed-write notice, the first-frame line — is fed nothing by the Filter, is bit-identical with the Filter on or off, and can never gleam, glide, tick-lie or go stale. The **reading register** is exactly six node families: the five suit readings (`suit.o2`, `suit.reserve`, `suit.integrity`, `suit.warmth`, `suit.charge`) and the scanner reading slot. Their glass, needle, fill and numeral pixels are the only lie-capable pixels in screen space, reached only through `perceived(SUIT_KEY(k), PlayerId)` and never through `true_value`. At MVP all six are honest (`READING_LIE_STAGE` is "never" for every key, and the scanner slot is an honest anchor whose own lie gate is `SCANNER_LIE_STAGE`, default never, stage 3 only); they are built with their dormant lie slots so Vertical Slice A can enable a lie without a redraw.
30	
31	**Index wording, reconciled.** The index (rationale bullet 21) reads: "HUD & Suit Layer (UI, MVP, explicit). Centre-bottom critical strip, bottom-left suit panel, hand rail, warning mark, tri-modal lying-reading signatures, HR-1..15. *Why this tier:* How the player reads their own body; Section 7 of the art bible specifies it." This GDD honours every noun of it and refines three: (1) "warning mark" is realised as one asset instantiated in per-reading slots beside the reading it concerns, not as a single object that "lives on the critical strip" (HS-21; the art bible 7.2 wording amendment is owed, Cross-References); (2) "tri-modal lying-reading signatures" is built at MVP as dormant, tested slots, with the charge cell's motion signature still open (Open Questions); (3) the reserve reading is added to the screen-space set (the art bible's HR-3 amendment is owed). **Numbering, once and for all:** this system is **Systems Enumeration row 21** and **Recommended Design Order 24**. The row marked `| 24 |` in the Systems Enumeration is Adaptive Audio & Tells, a different system.
32	
33	**The MVP slice and what waits.** **MVP (this GDD, playable solo):** the critical strip with the breath dial arc (ambient O2, or the reserve while it is engaged), pivot cap, three-digit numeral and one reserved mark slot; the suit panel with reserve (whole seconds), integrity (zone-band dial, no numeral), warmth (zone-band dial, no numeral), charge (cell fill) and the lamp-switch state; the hand rail (three tool slots in a four-slot geometry, glowstick 0-4, carried-module glyph, scanner reading slot, MVP-live and honest: an anchor per Sanity SN-19); the warning marks: five suit-rung slots plus the one-bit ship-alarm mark `suit.alarm` on its own panel slot (six slots, D89); the prompt plate (ENABLED and NEEDS_TOOL), the press acknowledgement, the linear bar at three length classes, hold-to-confirm; the failed-write notice (MVP-live on Save/Load's published `fail_escalated` read, HS-46) and the first-frame ship-log line (UI-7 after a fallback load; one plain record line after a `DEATH_STUB` restore, D15); the glyph-device swap; the `Theme` and shared components; the `HudSettings` hooks at their defaults; the dormant lie slots driven only by a stub Filter in tests. **Specified but dormant at MVP:** the gleam, glide, tick/stale and sound-request slots on all six reading families. **Vertical Slice A:** the suppressant tool returns to the fourth rail slot, with its charge pips, in the slice that adds its effect verb (X6); reading lies enabled through `READING_LIE_STAGE` (warmth first, then O2 and charge, then integrity and reserve), the scanner reading lying only behind `SCANNER_LIE_STAGE` (Sanity's, registered, default never, stage 3 only), the charge-cell motion signature, and the mark inheriting a lying reading's class. **Vertical Slice B:** the crew strip, chat and caption anchors (reserved, drawn by other systems), the own-identity glyph on the suit panel, the one-bit harm prompt on the ordinary plate, the name-reveal component. **Alpha:** the accessibility settings screens, HUD opacity (a hook at 100 % until then), pattern strength, captions. Nothing in this list adds a progression, an inventory screen, a weapon or a meter. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
34	
35	**What this GDD does not own** (scope guard, enforced as rules): the vitals ladder, rungs and hold times (Suit); whether, when and for whom a reading lies (Filter, Sanity); which verb a press means, when a prompt exists and how long a channel runs (Interaction, Controller); the layers, `H`, `world_to_hud`, `present_time`, pause rendering and the picture rect (Render Pipeline); the pause panel, web map and menus (Chart Table); every sound (Adaptive Audio); the failure count that raises the save notice (Save/Load); alarm eligibility and band tables (Life-Support Graph).
36	
37	*Implementation questions raised while designing and deferred to ADRs (-> `/architecture-decision`): (A) the widget approach — a `Control` scene tree versus one custom-draw surface per plate, and the `Theme` structure; (B) the two-clock policy for layer 2 (`present_time` for animation, the committed tick `T` for the mark, process time for layer 3); (C) the update model (a per-frame `HudModel` snapshot versus per-widget polling versus dirty-key subscription); (D) the bitmap instrument-face import pipeline and tabular-numeral enforcement; (E) the render-time clock source for the hold bar under pause; (F) the explicit per-frame presenter order (camera solver, Avatar Presenter, Filter, HUD, Lighting) so that `world_to_hud` and `perceived` are read after their producers; (G) the HUD maths as pure static functions so a headless test run can assert them. No ADR exists yet (`docs/architecture/` holds only `tr-registry.yaml`). The pinned engine reference (`docs/engine-reference/godot/`; domain file `modules/ui.md`, with `input.md`, `rendering.md` and `breaking-changes.md`) has **no `scripting.md` and no `core.md`**: GDScript typing, `_process` ordering, signal timing, canvas batching, text-measurement calls, cursor modes and bitmap-font import are NOT SOURCEABLE from it and are asserted nowhere in this GDD.*
38	
39	## Player Fantasy
40	
41	> **Design test first (P1):** *A hidden stat vs. a visibly leaking pipe → the pipe.* On a screen this reads: **if a vital can reach the player as a body cue or as a number, the body cue comes first and the number is its second opinion.** The HUD is the number.
42	
43	**Framing: direct.** The player experiences this system directly: it is the glass in front of their own eyes. *(creative-director consulted; three framings weighed and logged: A "The Visor" — a still frame you wear — is the headline, because it is the art bible's own governing rule, 7.0 "the HUD is a suit, the ship is an instrument", turned into a feeling; B "The Second Opinion" — the free rung of the falsifier ladder — is adopted as the HUD's role and cost layer, not its headline, because a headline of "the HUD checks the world" would make the numeral the fantasy and the numeral is the one surface architected to lie; C "The Survival Dashboard" — every vital as a bar or icon in a corner — is rejected: the art bible rejected it by name for violating Principle 2, the Suit rejected the moodle strip, and the user chose the centre-bottom strip over a corner cluster. A fully diegetic Dead-Space-style readout was rejected upstream and is not reopened.)*
44	
45	> It is the only light that is not in the world. A strip of dark glass at the bottom of your vision with your breath on it; a small panel at your left hip; your hands at your right. It does not glow, it does not shake, it does not tell you where you are or what is coming. It tells you about you.
46	>
47	> In the dark of a dead ship it is the one thing that stays exactly where it was. That is what it is for. When the hatch blows and the beam swings and your breath goes ragged, the frame has not moved a pixel, and the numeral on it is falling one step at a time. You read it without looking away from the cone.
48	>
49	> You trust it the way you trust a gauge you have watched agree with a pipe. Which is to say: you check.
50	
51	**The emotion named: held composure.** Not comfort and not power. The HUD's pleasure is *steadiness under fear* — the art bible's hardest test, "frightened, still reading", made into the player's experience. Its dread is quieter and arrives later (Vertical Slice A): the steadiest thing on screen is also the closest thing to you that can lie. The Suit names the body's emotion *competent fragility*; the HUD is the composure that lets the player act on it. The two fantasies are laid side by side, not stacked: the Suit owns the body ("The Body Is the Last Instrument"), the HUD is the screen side of the same moments, and this section restates none of the Suit's.
52	
53	**MDA mapping (concept ranking).** *Challenge* (2): the HUD serves reading competence — learning the three motion signatures (settle = honest change, tick = honest digit, glide / continuous tick = lie) is a mastery the game never explains in text. *Discovery* (1): served thinly and negatively — the HUD never shows what the world should reveal (no minimap, no room name, no ship state), so discovery stays in the beam. *Fantasy* (4): "we are the only ones awake" is helped by an interface that says nothing about the web. *Sensation* (6): restraint is the sensation — a still frame against a moving beam. *Self-determination:* Competence (the zone bands and the numeral are learnable and honest at MVP); Autonomy (the HUD never instructs: no objective, no tutorial overlay); Relatedness (Vertical Slice B: the crew strip carries no vitals, so checking on a friend means lighting them, not reading a bar).
54	
55	### Pillar table
56	
57	| Pillar | Role | How this system serves it | Design test it carries |
58	|---|---|---|---|
59	| **P1 The World Never Lies** | **PRIMARY** | The frame is an anchor, fed nothing by the Filter. The five readings are the only lie-capable surface in screen space. Everything else — prompts, bar, rail glyphs and counts, notices — is meta-register truth. No ship state, no minimap, no banner ("COOLANT LOW" is the banner Principle 2 rejected). The honest cross-check for a suit reading is the body and the room, never a second HUD element. | The pipe over the stat; the body cue first, the number its second opinion. |
60	| **P4 Sanity Rewrites Reality** | **PRIMARY (co-primary)** | Hosts the lie slots on all five readings and the scanner slot: violet gleam on the glass edge, one motion signature, a sound request — dormant at MVP. Carries no sanity meter, bar, ring, number, icon or colour anywhere, under any setting. The honest `suit.o2` numeral is the MVP's second instrument. | No lie is unfalsifiable; at least one channel of truth remains (on the visor: the body and the room). |
61	| **P2 Dread Before Chaos** | Serves | The mark fires only at CRITICAL after the hold (or at `CELL_WARN_S`), never at STRAINED, never first; one alarm rhythm shared with the beacon. Prompts and hold-to-confirm never shake, flash or announce. | The HUD is never the first channel of a failure. |
62	| **P3 The Web Watches** | Serves (negatively) | No Attention, noise, light-level, illumination, exposure, horror, proximity or direction indicator under any setting. Prompts exist only where Interaction says the object is lit, so "reach for it" stays a free falsifier. | A meter vs a world tell: the tell. |
63	| **P5 Deeper Is Richer, Loss Is Not Total** | Serves (through loss) | No death screen, no score, no restore beat beyond one plain ship-log line. A restore draws the readings at their restored values; the single record line (no death wording, HS-46) is the only trace *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. | Failure costs ship and body; the HUD adds no punishment text. |
64	
65	### Three design tests the section must be able to defend
66	
67	| # | Design test | Pillar served | Applied to the HUD |
68	|---|---|---|---|
69	| **HS-DT-1** | **The body first.** *A vital that reaches the player only as a reading vs one that reaches them first as a body cue → the body cue first; the reading is its second opinion.* | P1: "Pipes leak, frost forms, air hisses; the physical world is ground truth. Only instruments and perception can be wrong." Inherits the Suit's design test 1 by citation. | The HUD never carries a vital the body does not also carry (the one deliberate exclusion is integrity STRAINED, which the Suit carries by the zone band alone). No HUD element is the first channel of anything that can kill. |
70	| **HS-DT-2** | **Who produced the number decides where it is drawn.** *A value the ship produced vs one the suit produced vs one nobody in the fiction produced → world / visor / plate.* | P1 + P3: "Attention is shown in the world ... never as a hidden meter." | Ship state goes to the world, lit to be read. Suit telemetry goes to the visor, in the reading register (lie-capable). Prompts, keycaps, the bar and the notices are meta, in the plate register (never lie-capable). A proposed HUD element that cannot name its producer is cut. |
71	| **HS-DT-3** | **Still frame, moving reading.** *A HUD that moves, flashes, tints or rescales with the game's state vs a frame that never moves and readings that move inside it → the still frame.* | P4: the lie leaks *on a reading*, never in the frame. P2: the mark has one rhythm. | Anything that moves the frame (shake, jolt, scale, blur, vignette, tint) is a defect, not a style choice. This is what makes a gliding needle readable rather than merely unsettling. |
72	
73	*Validation proposal (playtest, not a constant):* HS-DT-1 holds if, in the MVP door-breach playtest, at least 6 of 8 testers asked "what told you the air was going?" answer with the breath or the valve click before the numeral (sound arm) and at least 4 of 8 in the muted arm, each judged on its own bar (OQ-HS-86) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: "most" had no N)*. If they answer "the number", the body cues are under-mixed or the HUD is too loud (route to the audio-director and ux-designer). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **The test needs a muted arm:** the fantasy depends on audio body cues coming first, yet the concept excludes adaptive audio from the MVP while the systems index lists it (row 24), so a failure could be misattributed to the HUD. The playtest therefore runs with sound and muted, each judged against its own pass criterion, and all three body cues (breath cadence, valve click, visor fog) ship in the MVP (resolved by user ruling, OQ-HS-67). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
74	
75	### Anchor moment (solo MVP): the door breach, from the screen's side
76	
77	This reuses the Suit's door-breach timeline so the two GDDs describe one moment, not two. All times are the Suit's illustrative values; the HUD adds no timing of its own. The keys are real.
78	
79	| t (s) (Suit's table) | Body / world (not the HUD's) | What the visor shows | The feeling targeted |
80	|---|---|---|---|
81	| 0 | hatch latch; draught, hiss | Nothing new. The O2 numeral (`perceived(SUIT_KEY(suit.o2), PlayerId)`, honest at MVP) begins to **tick** down at its hold grid; the strip's dial arc **settles** after each change. No mark, no text, no colour change. | The world speaks first. The HUD's first act is to stay quiet. |
82	| ~2.5 | breath quickens (STRAINED, the first body cue) | The needle crosses a zone tick on the arc. Still no mark: STRAINED never fires the mark. | "My breathing changed — the number agrees." The number is the second opinion. |
83	| ~6.4 | **valve click**, breath goes close and dry, visor fog | **The strip's breath dial swaps to the reserve** (`breath_src` becomes RESERVE, HS-12), on the render frame the HUD reads the new source: the numeral now reads whole seconds of reserve (starting at the reserve level, `RESERVE_S` 90 when full), the needle re-targets to permille of `RESERVE_S` and settles, the engraved tank tick and warn notch light and the dkPa zone ticks dim to Graphite; the ambient O2 numeral moves to the panel's ambient slot and keeps ticking on the same grid; the panel's reserve cell shows the same seconds and its underlay. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; Resolved 2026-10-27 — re-review, G2; the earlier row kept the ambient reading on the strip through the reserve leg, which left a dead ambient 0 at the glance point while the number that keeps you alive sat in the periphery)* | The click told you; the dial you are already reading now tells you how long. |

"Rarity is the signal": the HUD never shows a mark the Suit and Graph have not published. |
85	| ~76 | stagger, walk-only (CRITICAL after `RUNG_MIN_TICKS`) | **The warning mark** appears beside the strip's breath dial, which is showing the reserve (the breath rung is CRITICAL, HS-12, HS-22) and, because the reserve is engaged, also beside the reserve reading on the panel (HS-22); both pulse in the one beacon phase (`BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS`); at the first-launch default (reduce flashing ON, D79) they are held solid instead (HS-23). It is the second Alarm Red of the sortie, after the panel's ship-alarm mark (row ~12.5). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* | Rarity is the signal. 86	| ~141 | DEAD (`DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS`) | Readings freeze. No death screen, no score, no text. | Death is a bitch. It happens. |
87	| restore | Save/Load restarts at the last autosave | On the first `RUNNING` frame the readings are drawn at their restored values: no settle, no abort frame, no notch; one plain ship-log line (no death wording, HS-46) is the only trace of the restore. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | You lost the interval, not the lesson (P5). The HUD does not grieve for you. |
88	
89	**The second anchor — the HUD's best MVP beat, and it costs nothing (Framing B).** The MVP's one hallucination class is false states on **ship** instruments. On a low-sanity run, a derelict's wall O2 gauge, lit in your beam, sits steady in its normal zone. Your breath is quick and shallow. Your strip numeral reads a value inside THIN and is still ticking down. The suit is honest at MVP (`READING_LIE_STAGE` "never"), so the strip **is** the second instrument that falsifies the wall (Sanity's rung table: an honest `suit.o2` or `suit.warmth` reading of the seat's current compartment is free to read). You believe your own glass and your breath together, and you walk out. *Design consequence carried into Acceptance Criteria:* `displayed_value == view.o2_pp_dkpa == compartment p_o2` in a THIN fixture. If the HUD is ever the one that is wrong at MVP, the MVP's single hallucination class has no cheap check.
90	
91	### Under hallucination the fantasy deepens, it does not break (Vertical Slice A; dormant at MVP)
92	
93	The split is the art bible's 7.0 table applied to the screen. The left column is guaranteed by construction (fed nothing by the Filter; bit-identical frame with the Filter on or off). The right column reaches the HUD only through `perceived(SUIT_KEY(k), PlayerId)` per render frame, never cached.
94	
95	| Cannot lie on the HUD (frame / meta register) | Can lie (reading register; Vertical Slice A at the earliest, through the Filter only) |
96	|---|---|
97	| The frame: plates, bezels, chamfers, rivets, geometry, position, scale | The O2 numeral and the strip arc's glass (`suit.o2`) |
98	| Prompt plates, keycaps, verb text, anchor tab, NEEDS_TOOL notch | The reserve numeral (`suit.reserve`) |
99	| The linear bar with needle-mark (the actor's own elapsed time) | The integrity dial (`suit.integrity`) |
100	| Tool glyphs, the equipped-tool bracket and glowstick count (rail counts are anchors; the suppressant's pips return with the tool, X6) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | The warmth dial (`suit.warmth`) |
101	| The lamp **switch** state on the charge row | The charge cell fill (`suit.charge`) |
102	| The failed-write notice and the first-frame line | The scanner reading slot |
103	| The warning mark's *shape and rhythm* | Whether a suit-rung mark shows beside a **lying** reading (it inherits its reading's class; the Graph-driven ship-alarm mark never lies, HS-30) |
104	
105	**How each lie leaks (tri-modal: the "subtle is allowed; absent is not" rule from P1).** Every lying reading carries the violet gleam on its own glass (fringe `#B07BE6`, never core), one motion signature, and a sound slot (Audio's). The strip's O2 lie rides the numeral (continuous **tick** or **stale-hold**) plus the gleam on the arc glass; **glide** lives on a suit-panel dial whose needle meets the eligibility floor (`NEEDLE_LEN_MIN_PX`, owned by In-World Instruments).
106	
107	**The deepening beat.** In a cold derelict at low sanity, the warmth dial's needle on the suit panel drifts upward — slow, smooth, never quite at rest — with a violet hairline on its glass. The frame around it has not moved. Your breath is smoking in your own cone and you are shivering. The HUD has not broken; one needle inside a still frame has detached from the body, and the stillness of everything else is exactly what lets you see it. *You believe the shiver. You go home.* That is P4's design test passed: the lie costs time and light to disprove, and it can always be disproved.
108	
109	**What the player learns, never told in text:** "needles that wander are lying; needles that shake are warning; numerals that step are honest." On the visor, tremor is not used on suit readings, so the vocabulary reduces to *settle and step* (honest) versus *glide and continuous tick or stale* (lie).
110	
111	**The hard edge, stated plainly.** At Vertical Slice A a lying suit reading can lie its rung mark away (a suit-rung mark inherits its reading's class, HS-30; the Graph-driven ship-alarm mark cannot be lied away). The fantasy accepts this because P4 promises "at least one channel of truth always remains", and on the visor that channel is the body (breath, click, fog, rime, stagger) and the room. The HUD must never be designed as if a suit-rung mark were an independent honest backup.
112	
113	**What hallucination never does to the HUD:** no vignette, tint, blur, glitch, scan-line, shake, chromatic aberration or scale change; no sanity number, bar, ring, icon or colour; no "lies spotted" count; no true value beside a lying one outside the Debug Overlay. A screen effect says "the HUD is broken"; the pillar says "the gauge is wrong".
114	
115	### Tone and language
116	
117	**Inherit the Suit's use/avoid list by citation** (suit, seal, breath, reserve, valve, cell, chest lamp, beam, go dark, visor, fog, rime, shiver, stagger, the hand, the rail, stow, the haul; never *health, HP, stamina, oxygen meter, O2 bar, encumbrance, inventory, flashlight, battery* for the suit's store, *vignette, tunnel vision, blur*). **HUD vocabulary (use):** visor, glass, strip (critical strip), panel (suit panel), rail (hand rail), plate (Ground plate), bezel, chamfer, rivet, keycap, bracket, dial arc, needle, pivot cap, zone band, numeral, the mark (warning mark), settle, tick, step, glide, gleam, stale, linear bar with needle-mark, prompt plate, anchor tab, cut (for removal). **Avoid** (the stale-token lint applies to this prose too): ring / radial / wipe / pie / circle as a UI shape ("ring clamp" and "depth rings" excepted), meter for anything that is not an instrument, bar except "linear bar", icon-as-state, toast, banner, popup, notification as a UI noun, widget in fantasy prose, HP, health bar, damage number, alert, threat, awareness, light level, exposure, lit state, minimap, compass, objective, quest, and "hand point" as a beam origin (the beam origin is the chest point). **Register.** Fantasy prose: second person, present tense, terse, physical. On screen: the instrument face for numerals and frame labels; the reading face only for the two meta lines (the failed-write notice and the first-frame line). **No warning words on screen, ever** — the mark is a glyph, not text, and Alarm Red is never text. Prompt verbs are verbs, not states ("Weld", "Cut away", "Install", "Drop"). No exclamation, no heroics, no system voice addressing the player.
118	
119	**Death-language deny-list (user ruling X8, no death wording on screen).** Lint list `HUD_DEATH_WORDS` (data, case-insensitive, whole-word and stem): die, dies, died, dying, dead, death, deadly, kill, killed, lose, lost, fatal, perish, expire, game over, respawn, revive (the last because solo has none at MVP). Applied to every HUD string key, in particular `plate_give_up` (English placeholder "Give up", HS-42(b)), `line_record_restored` (HS-46), `notice_save_failed` and `verb_confirm_prompt`. Verbs are the Controller's action name or plain verbs; the plate says nothing about what happens next. Tested by AC-HS-147 (d). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*
120	
121	### Reference techniques: adopt and reject
122	
123	The Suit's reference table (Pandorum, Zomboid, Metro, Dead Space, Subnautica, Barotrauma, Death Stranding, Don't Starve, Beyond the Aquila Rift) is cited, not restated. HUD-specific rows:
124	
125	| Reference | Adopt | Reject |
126	|---|---|---|
127	| **Apollo Command Module main console** (the art bible's HUD touchstone) | The meter's grammar: a thin moving needle inside a static engraved housing with a marked safe zone — frame versus reading at a glance; one reserved annunciator for every alarm (our single warning mark, one rhythm). | Switch density and the continuous panel plane (our HUD is a few small plates, about 1 % non-Ground area); cool internal panel light (collides with O2 Cyan); period nostalgia. |
128	| **Project Zomboid** (the user's touchstone) | Restraint: the world, not the UI, is where you learn you are in trouble; discrete named states that escalate in steps; zoom in and out with a HUD that does not rescale. | The moodle column as the primary channel; any status icon for hunger, fatigue or panic; any "panic" UI response to fear. |
129	| **Pandorum** | The chest lamp as the player's own equipment: the HUD shows its **switch** and **charge**, never what it illuminates. | A hand-held light on the rail. |
130	| **Metro 2033 / Exodus** | The wrist-watch filter timer: a reading worn on the body and consulted, while breath and visor fog are the alarm. Our reserve numeral in whole seconds is that watch. | Mask-wipe and filter-swap chores. |
131	| **Alien: Isolation** (motion tracker) | Nothing on the HUD. Its lesson is negative: a device that tells you where the threat is replaces dread with a radar. | Any proximity, direction, threat or "they are near" surface. |
132	| **Dead Space** | Already rejected as a full model; adopt only the idea that the HUD belongs to the suit, not the game. | Holographic UI that floats in the world; a health spine painted on a body. |
133	| **Subnautica** | The O2 numeral as a plain reading of a real reserve. | The radial O2 gauge (radial is banned) and instant-blackout-at-zero presentation. |
134	| **Genre-default screen effects for sanity or injury** | — | Vignette, desaturation, blur, screen tint for any state. Sanity never reads off the screen's energy. |
135	| **Beyond the Aquila Rift** | The kind lie with one physical detail that betrays it: the warmth needle's calm drift against the shiver. | Any HUD "reveal" (glitch-out, frame cracking, text corruption) — an authored story beat and a screen effect. |
136	
137	### Anti-pillar guard rails (the fantasy's limits)
138	
139	1. **Not a combat game.** No health bar, hit flash, damage number, threat bar, lock-on, kill count or reticle (the one exception is the opt-in, off-by-default accessibility aim indicator, HS-52, which draws a direction only, never a target) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. The suppressant (Vertical Slice; not in the MVP kit, X6) shows its charges as a reading, never as ammunition. Integrity is a dial with zone bands, never a health number.
140	2. **Not a freeform builder.** No inventory screen, grid, weight readout, capacity or "slots free" count, mass bar or encumbrance indicator; the rail is four tools, two counts and the carried-module glyph. The weld prompt is a verb, not a build menu.
141	3. **Not intentional PvP.** No crewmate vitals, sanity sign or harm counter on any HUD surface. The one-bit harm prompt (Vertical Slice B, reserved) is the actor's own honest self-knowledge drawn on the ordinary plate: no red, no tell, no roster flag.
142	4. **Not an authored story.** No toast, banner, log pop-up, objective, quest marker or narrative text. The only text lines are meta (the failed-write notice and the first-frame line), plain, without cause or drama.
143	5. **Not a game you win.** No progress indicator, completion percentage, depth score, run timer or "time aboard" counter.
144	6. **P3 negative contract.** No Attention, noise, light-level, illumination, exposure, horror, proximity or direction indicator under any setting, including accessibility.
145	7. **P4 negative contract.** No sanity meter, bar, ring, number, icon or colour, anywhere, under any setting; the only violet in screen space is the gleam on a lying reading's glass.
146	8. **P1 frame contract.** The frame is an anchor: never shaken, jolted, tinted, blurred, rescaled or lie-capable. Ship state is never on the HUD (no room name, no loop summary).
147	9. **P2 rhythm contract.** The HUD is never the first warning of anything; the mark fires only at CRITICAL (after the hold) or `CELL_WARN_S`, never at STRAINED, in one beacon phase.
148	10. **P5 failure contract.** No death screen, no score, no restore beat on the HUD beyond the one plain ship-log line of HS-46 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
149	
150	**The forbidden-surface list** (carried as a lint into Acceptance Criteria): a minimap, compass, objective marker, quest log, off-screen arrow, crew locator, ship-status or loop summary, room name, weight / capacity / inventory, health bar, Attention / noise / light meter, sanity meter / icon / colour, horror indicator, vignette, screen-edge tint, damage number, hit flash, kill or score, death screen, progress toast, loading spinner, autosave glyph, "repaired" toast, a countdown to an event the HUD names (the reserve numeral is a plain reading of the suit's own store and names no event, HS-17), or any text in Alarm Red.
151	
152	**The feel word for the whole layer is *machined*:** things step, settle and stop. Nothing bounces, pops or scales; "juicy UI" is rejected by the art bible.
153

1147	
1148	The art bible section 7 (7.0 "the HUD is a suit, the ship is an instrument", 7.1 to 7.3, and the hard requirements HR-1 to HR-15 of 7.7) is the spec of record; this section turns it into per-event visual rows, a palette rule set, a geometry table, a lie-slot specification and an asset inventory. The art-director was consulted (proposal reconciled below; where a figure in that proposal had been overtaken by a ruling, the ruling's figure is used and the change is noted in line). Row ids are `HSV-n`. "HUD px" is one pixel of the HUD canvas (`H` screen px, Pipeline D.4); at `H_default` on a 1080p screen it equals one base art px, so the art bible's "art px" and the HUD px coincide at the default and nothing re-authors at higher `H`. 1170	### Truth-channel classification
1171	
1172	Every visual the HUD emits is outside the Graph's closed **consequence channel** (the HUD writes nothing to the simulation and neither adds nor removes a consequence cue). Within the HUD there are **four classes** (A, M, T, R; the earlier text said three while listing four) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*:
1173	
1174	- **ANCHOR (A):** never shifts under hallucination; fed nothing by the Filter; the HR-6 list; bit-identical with the Filter on or off.
1175	- **META-TRUTH (M):** honest by definition, in the meta register; never lie-capable (no gleam, glide, tick or stale). Prompts, the channel bar (the actor's own elapsed time) and the two notices.
1176	- **TRUTH READING (T):** a Graph-driven one-bit reading drawn in a mark slot (the ship-alarm mark `suit.alarm`, accepted at MVP by user ruling D89, HS-25, HS-30) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. 1177	- **READING (R):** lie-capable instrument pixels, fed by `perceived(SUIT_KEY(k), PlayerId)` or `perceived(SCANNER, PlayerId)` every render frame and never cached. Nothing else on the frame is above 61. Alarm Red (about 47) is the mark and is distinguished by shape and the Paper White stroke inside it, not by lightness.
1223	- **L-2. Greyscale pairs each need a shape backup.** Paper White (about 90) against Tungsten (about 85): the bracket, the bezel thickening and the position (equipped tool); the needle-mark overhang (bar). Alarm Red (about 47) against Graphite lit (about 43) against the violet core (about 43): a chamfered *filled* square with a Paper White stroke, a 1-px hairline, and an edge gleam. O2 Cyan against Paper White: a glyph against ink, never adjacent in the same role.
1224	- **L-3. State by luminance and position, not by tint.** A reading never changes colour with its value; a zone crossing moves the needle against fixed engraving. No red numeral, no amber numeral, no flashing numeral. This is what keeps the HUD from becoming a health bar (anti-pillar: not a combat game).
1225	- **L-4. Warmth never borrows a hue.** Cold would invite Coolant Ice and hot would invite Fuel Ember or Alarm Red; using them would assert that heat is a loop and would spend Alarm Red as decoration. The warmth dial is Paper White ink with pattern-coded zones (cold left, hot right).
1226	- **L-5. Dead is Graphite lit.** A reading whose source is dead (no breathable source; reserve at zero) draws its glyph and strip arc band in Graphite lit while the needle and numeral stay Paper White because they are the reading, not the loop. The change is a hard cut counted once in the flash budget, not a periodic event.

1436	## Game Feel
1437	
1438	The HUD is a screen the player reads, not a thing they steer, so its "feel" is the quality of three promises: it answers a press instantly, it never moves unless the world did, and it never performs. Every target below is a number so a tester can pass or fail it. Ids are `GF-HS-n` (the rulings set no prefix for this section; this one is chosen so a story can cite a feel target by id). Units: ticks at `TICK_RATE` 60 (1 tick = 16.67 ms), render frames at the display rate (60 fps assumed; 30 fps is the supported floor and is noted where it matters), HUD px (one pixel of the HUD canvas = `H` screen px), and milliseconds of `present_time` (frozen under pause, HS-8). All values here are the HUD's own `[PH]` knobs or cited from their owners; none changes a simulation value.
1439	
1440	### Feel pillars for this system (what the numbers serve)
1441	
1442	- **Cuts, not tweens (art bible 7.3).** The only interpolations on the HUD are the dial-needle settle and the cosmetic hold-bar drain. Everything else, including every numeral change, glyph change, tool switch, mark edge, plate show and plate hide, is a hard cut within one render frame. Weight comes from mass and stillness, not from motion: the HUD never shakes, pops, flashes, pulses a reading, scales, or fades.
1443	- **The HUD is quiet when the world is loud (P2).** In a breach the screen's own changes are bounded by `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` 3 luminance events per rolling second; a player under pressure is never made to parse a flickering HUD (HR-13).
1444	- **Snap means whole HUD px.** Every edge, stroke, bar cell and plate position lands on a whole HUD px at the current integer `H`; a plate follows its subject by `floor(world_to_hud(anchor_o))` from the **unjolted** camera pose, so camera jolt and hit-shake move the world and never the HUD (zero px of HUD shake, by construction).
1445

1449	|---|---|---|---|---|
1450	| 1. Press | The player presses `interact` (key or pad button); the Adapter applies it as a command at the next tick | Press to command application: at most 1 tick (16.7 ms), the Controller's and kernel's | Controller / kernel | The HUD does not own this step |
1451	| 2. ACK (pre-play) | On the **same render frame as the accepted press** the keycap face drops 1 px and the bar track appears at fill 0 (Adapter-local, never a simulation state, HS-41) | At most 1 render frame after the press (16.7 ms at 60 fps; 33 ms at 30 fps) | HUD | A press must feel received before the sim has answered |
1452	| 3. Result | The simulation confirms (`CONFIRMED`) or rejects within `PREPLAY_MAX_TICKS` 2 (33 ms) | At most 2 ticks | Interaction | A confirm keeps the pre-play; silence withdraws it |
1453	| 3a. Reject | The pre-play is withdrawn; the restored keycap is held Graphite-lit for `BAR_REJECT_HOLD_TICKS` 9; no shake, flash, red or text; identical for every reason *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | At most 1 render frame after the reject arrives, then 9 ticks | HUD | Rejection is quiet, not an event |

1456	| 5b. Abort (`ended_by` `WORLD`) | Fill snaps empty; a 2 x 2 Ground break-notch is held `BAR_HOLD_DONE_TICKS` 12 (200 ms), then the bar withdraws; the same frame set for every world cause *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | 12 ticks | HUD | Breaking is seen once and not explained |
1457	| 5c. Player cancel (a channel `PLAYER_CANCEL`; a hold-to-confirm release is the Controller's `b`) | The fill drains right to left over `BAR_DRAIN_MS` 400 from any fill and any length class (D.16); a hold release follows the Controller's `b` (0.4 s from full on SHORT); reduced motion snaps to 0 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the row kept the retired drain scaled by `CONFIRM_DRAIN_RATE` times the fill speed)* | 0.4 s for every length class | HUD (cosmetic) | A channel cancel is keyed off `ended_by` = `PLAYER_CANCEL` (CF-HS-17, answered); the hold-to-confirm release stays provisional on the Controller's hold read (CF-HS-16) |

1461	**Sim-to-screen latency of a reading.** The HUD pulls its five `perceived` records every render frame (HS-7) and is last in the presenter order (camera solver, Avatar Presenter, Filter, HUD, Lighting). A value committed at tick `T` is therefore drawn on the first render frame after the commit: worst case 1 tick (16.7 ms) plus 1 render frame (16.7 ms) = 33 ms at 60 fps. The numeral then additionally waits for the next grid boundary (below); the needle starts its settle on that same frame.

1490	### Weight and snap
1491	
1492	- **Weight.** A frame is heavy by mass and still; a reading is light by thin bright strokes and motion (art bible 3.4). No HUD element has easing except the needle settle and the cosmetic drain; there is no ease-in, ease-out, bounce, slide, wipe, scale-pop or fade anywhere. A needle never overshoots (the settle is monotone, D.6). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
1493	- **Snap.** Placement is integer HUD px at every `H` (D.9): at the Deck's 1280 x 800 with `H` 3 over `k` 2 the canvas is 426.67 x 240 HUD px, every rectangle is floored to a whole HUD px and the 2-screen-px remainder is split evenly as margin. The bar fills in whole cells (`floor(progress_pm x L / 1000)`), never a partial pixel. A needle's tip lands on a whole HUD px (35 / 51 / 76 pre-baked frames at `L` 11 / 16 / 24 at the 180-degree sweep, D.15; 68 and 101 are the 240-degree counts for `L` 16 and 24, a formula case only) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
1494	- **Input can make the HUD no louder than the ceiling through its state displays, and every acknowledgement is bounded and recorded** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the earlier sentence promised that no input raises the HUD above the ceiling, which HS-47's counted-never-deferred events falsified)*. Spamming `interact` is bounded by `PROMPT_MIN_CYCLE_TICKS`; cycling tools at 10 Hz, throwing sticks, toggling the lamp ten times a second and tapping the TAP-mode confirm all pass the one shared state-display limiter (at most one drawn change per `GLYPH_STATE_LATCH_TICKS` 20 across the class, so at most 3 a second, each showing the latest state); no deferrable event can exceed `FLASH_MAX_PER_S`; the acknowledgement cues (ACK dip with its force-admitted plate, reject hold, OUTCOME border) are counted, rate-gated and may overrun a full window, and an overrun is recorded as `HUD_FLASH_OVERRUN`, never hidden (AC-HS-72, AC-HS-140).
1495	- **Stillness at rest.** With all readings OK, no prompt, no mark and no notice, no HUD pixel changes from one render frame to the next except a numeral substitution on a real change; the at-rest picture is a held breath (Player Fantasy: held composure).
